9:T513,The paper is a controlled empirical study rather than a new architecture paper. It fixes total training tokens at each active-parameter scale and varies the amount of unique data, which directly changes the repetition rate. Dense Transformers are compared with multiple MoE configurations across 80M, 200M, and 1B active parameters, with the largest configuration reaching 8.5B total parameters. The MoE sweep varies expert count, expert granularity, and sparsity. Expert granularity refers to the width of each expert FFN relative to the dense FFN; compute-matched MoEs often use a granularity of 1/k when k experts are active per token. The data sweep covers single-domain corpora and mixed-domain settings, including web, code, scientific, and encyclopedic text, with both filtered and unfiltered variants. Beyond held-out loss, the paper analyzes domain-local degradation, regularization, router stability, expert activation patterns, and expert specialization. A key mechanistic finding is that router assignments stabilize early in training. After that point, each expert updates on a relatively small and nearly stationary subset of tokens. Repeating the corpus therefore repeats the same expert-specific token subsets, making sparse experts more prone to narrow memorization than dense FFNs.a:T4ee,The empirical pattern is consistent across scales and domains. On unique data, MoEs outperform dense models. As repetition increases, MoEs degrade earlier: at the 80M scale, dense models remain relatively robust until beyond roughly 8x repetition, while MoEs show clear degradation at 4x repetition. By 32x repetition, MoEs lose their advantage over dense models. The severity increases with sparsity and is better predicted by total parameter count than by active parameter count. Data quality filtering changes the magnitude but not the direction of the effect; some unfiltered settings overfit more, but filtering does not remove the MoE-specific sensitivity to repeated data. In mixed-domain training, degradation is mostly confined to the repeated domains, and non-repeated tokens from other domains provide some regularization. Among regularization methods, dropout and output masking are effective, especially for MoEs, while some other standard methods help little. With sufficiently high dropout, MoEs can still outperform dense models even at 64x repetition. Mechanistic measurements show early router stabilization and increased expert specialization under repetition, supporting the interpretation that repeated data is amplified at the expert level.b:T400,The technical idea is to replace inferred membership labels with exact-match copy counts. The paper queries infini-gram indexes over OLMo-mix-1124 and the Pile to obtain the number of times a sentence appears in each corpus. These counts are conservative floors: punctuation changes, quote normalization, line breaks, and unindexed annealing data are not counted. The central design compares the same sentence across two model families. If a sentence appears more often in the OLMo corpus than in the Pile, the test asks whether an OLMo-2 model assigns it lower loss than a Pythia model, and vice versa. Because the sentence is identical, fluency, length, author quality, and wording are held fixed. The paper also evaluates standard loss-based detectors across copy-count regimes, tests one-word edited controls, and swaps in controls with different register. The purpose is not to build a stronger attack, but to isolate which parts of the apparent signal come from exposure and which parts come from evaluation artifacts.c:T52c,The experiments use five models from the OLMo-2 and Pythia families, ranging from 1B to 13B parameters. For ordinary sentences with 1 to 1,000 copies, loss-based membership evidence is nearly flat within noise. A 1B model reaches about 0.60 AUC on ordinary sentences, while famous lines with a median of roughly 1,200 copies reach 0.83 AUC. In the same-sentence design, using 747 sentences and within-book comparisons, the rank correlation between relative exposure and relative loss is about −0.08 for 7B models and −0.07 for 13B models, where −1 would be a perfect exposure-lowers-loss relationship and 0 means no relationship. This accounts for less than one percent of variance and does not strengthen with scale. One-word edits are shown to be poor non-member controls: in more than 90% of pairs, the original sentence has lower loss than the edit, by about 0.4 nats per token, or roughly 1.5× average token probability. The gap is similar whether the original appeared once or a hundred times, indicating that it measures wording quality rather than memory. Above about 1,000 copies, the gap grows with model size on the twelve available sentences. Changing controls from same-source edits to composed-prose controls moves AUC from 0.83 to 0.94, showing that register mismatch can manufacture a strong detector.d:T4ee,WPMIA replaces token-level likelihood (unavailable) with an estimable word-level likelihood derived from Monte Carlo sampling.

1) Word-level probability estimation: represent the target text as a sequence of words. For each position, query the model multiple times conditioned on the preceding words, collect sampled continuations, and estimate P(next_word = w_t | prefix) by frequency. Local kernel smoothing is applied to reduce variance and avoid brittle zero counts under finite sampling.

2) Sequence-level likelihood estimator: aggregate the estimated word probabilities via a chain-rule style log-likelihood (typically mean log-likelihood) to obtain a membership score that mirrors classic likelihood-based MIAs.

3) Prefix-conditioned contrast: build two conditioning contexts (member-like vs non-member-like prefixes) and estimate the sequence likelihood under each, then contrast them to amplify the membership gap. A notable design choice is to contrast at the sequence level (after aggregation) instead of taking unstable word-level probability ratios.

4) Practical threat model: explicitly assumes the attacker does not know the target tokenizer, motivating word-level modeling; relies only on text sampling, matching typical proprietary LLM APIs.e:T9ab,方法是一个四阶段合成流水线，重点在于把原本分散的控制信号统一进同一份脚本。

第一阶段生成 persona 和 scenario。作者先用 DeepSeek-v4.1-pro 构造 persona seed pool 和 topic/scenario seed pool，再扩展成双人对话设定。设定里不仅有姓名、性别、年龄、职业、性格、角色，还包含 scene、tone、narrative type、scene medium、三段式事件链和分段情绪弧线。这里的关键不是“让 LLM 写对话”，而是先把约束条件结构化，减少后续脚本生成时的人设漂移和场景不一致。

第二阶段生成脚本。Gemini-3.1-pro-preview 根据前面的结构化设定写 spoken-style dialogue，并在脚本中显式插入三类标签：全双工行为标签（interrupt、backchannel、incomplete）、情绪标签（7 类，和 IndexTTS2 支持的情绪集合对齐）、环境声/事件声标签。这样做的好处是后续语音合成和音频装配不需要再做复杂推断，脚本本身就是多通道控制接口。

第三阶段做表达性语音合成和双轨装配。作者选 IndexTTS2，是因为它支持 timbre 与 emotion 的解耦控制。64 个说话人音色覆盖 13 类 persona 和 5 个年龄桶。每个 utterance 先单独合成，再做 forced alignment 得到词级时间戳，然后按说话人分别拼成两条长语音轨。全双工行为不是靠重新生成语音，而是在装配阶段实现：incomplete 用文本中的“...”触发句内停顿；interrupt 通过一方淡出、另一方提前切入制造重叠；backchannel 则把短回应叠加到另一方持续说话的轨道上。这个设计很工程化，但优点是行为控制明确、可批量生成。

第四阶段注入背景声和事件声。每个说话通道配一个背景通道，背景由环境噪声和短时事件声组成。环境噪声来自 7 类场景、600 段长音频；事件声来自 52 类、2203 段短音频。事件声按脚本中的触发词和词级时间戳对齐，再控制 SNR 注入。这样得到的不是简单的“语音+噪声”，而是和语义位置绑定的声学事件。

最后还有质量验证器。论文强调会过滤脚本和音频质量不达标的样本，并使用双 LLM judge 做脚本合理性复核。这个 validator 是数据集可信度的重要部分，但从全文可见，真正决定数据质量的仍是前面各阶段约束是否足够强，以及 LLM judge 的偏差是否会把风格统一化。f:Ta07,The method is a four-stage synthesis pipeline, with the central idea of turning the script into a unified control interface for multiple acoustic factors.

Stage 1 builds structured persona-scenario tuples. Using DeepSeek-v4.1-pro, the authors first create persona and topic seed pools, then expand them into two-speaker dialogue setups under consistency constraints. These setups include speaker attributes, scene, tone, narrative type, scene medium, a three-event progression chain, and an emotional arc. This matters because it separates high-level consistency control from later script realization.

Stage 2 generates dialogue scripts with explicit tags. Gemini-3.1-pro-preview writes spoken-style dialogues conditioned on the structured setup, while inserting three orthogonal tag families: duplex behavior tags (interrupt, backchannel, incomplete), emotion tags aligned with IndexTTS2’s supported emotions, and environmental/sound-event tags. This is a strong design choice: instead of inferring behavior during audio generation, the script already specifies what should happen.

Stage 3 performs expressive TTS and two-track assembly. The authors use IndexTTS2 because it supports disentangled control over speaker timbre and emotion. They synthesize each utterance separately, run forced alignment to obtain word-level timestamps, and then assemble two long-form speaker tracks. Duplex behaviors are realized during assembly rather than by training a specialized overlap synthesizer: incomplete utterances are rendered via ellipsis-induced pauses, interruptions are created by fading one speaker out while bringing the other in early, and backchannels are overlaid on top of the other speaker’s continuing speech. This is a pragmatic engineering solution with clear controllability.

Stage 4 injects background noise and sound events. Each speaker channel is paired with a background channel composed of environmental noise and short sound events. Environmental clips come from a 7-category bank; sound events come from a 52-category bank. Events are aligned to trigger words using the word-level timestamps from forced alignment, with controlled SNR. This makes the non-speech audio semantically grounded rather than random augmentation.

A quality validator filters low-quality dialogues before release, and the paper also uses dual LLM judges for script rationality checks. That improves reliability, although the final quality still depends heavily on how strong the upstream constraints are and how much the LLM judges bias the retained distribution.10:T647,The dataset scale is the main empirical result. The full generated corpus exceeds 2,000 hours. The released subset contains 6,400 bilingual dialogues totaling about 800 hours, with roughly 500 hours in Chinese and 300 hours in English. The voice pool has 64 timbres spanning 13 persona types and 5 age buckets. About 3.8% of all turns contain at least one duplex behavior. The release also includes 600 environmental audio clips, 2,203 sound-event clips, and the prompts used for LLM-based script evaluation.

The experimental section is less about benchmark competition and more about validating that the synthesis pipeline produces trainable data. The paper reports script-quality checks, audio-quality checks, and internal full-duplex model training validation, suggesting that the generated corpus is usable for model training.

For a pretraining researcher, the more interesting takeaways are indirect. First, explicit script tags appear sufficient to drive stable realization of overlap, backchannel, and incomplete speech. Second, word-level alignment turns sound-event injection into semantically anchored audio rather than generic noise augmentation. Third, persona and emotion can be jointly controlled at the TTS stage, which suggests a path toward using these factors as explicit conditioning variables in future speech LM pipelines. What remains less clear is how close these synthetic behaviors are to natural conversational distributions, whether models trained on them overfit to synthesis artifacts, and whether a 3.8% duplex-behavior rate is enough for strong real-time interaction skills.11:T487,This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction and the pipeline figure to understand the four-stage design. Then read the script-generation, audio-assembly, and sound-event injection sections carefully, because that is where the actual contribution sits. Finish with the quality-validation and dataset-statistics sections to judge whether the corpus is usable as a training asset. About 20–30 minutes should be enough.

Three details deserve attention. First, why the authors structure persona and scenario before script generation; that choice is important for scalability and consistency. Second, how each duplex behavior is realized acoustically during assembly; this determines whether the labels map cleanly to observable audio phenomena. Third, how the validator works and how the dual LLM judges are used, because that will shape the final retained distribution.

If your work is in speech LM or spoken dialogue pretraining, the natural follow-up questions are whether these explicit tags can be converted into a unified token stream for a single LM, and how synthetic duplex data should be mixed with natural conversational audio during training.12:T9e1,技术方案分成两层：模块化 tokenizer 构造，以及与之配套的预训练策略。

先看 tokenizer。作者分别给出 modular BPE 和 modular Unigram 的构造方法，目标是训练一个“大而可拆”的 multilingual tokenizer，然后从中抽取任意语言子集对应的 subtokenizer。这里难点不只是把不同语言的词表拼起来，因为简单拼接会破坏 token id、merge 规则或概率结构的一致性，也不保证抽出来的子词表还能接近单语 tokenizer 的压缩率。论文的做法是从训练阶段就约束 tokenizer 的结构，使每种语言或语言组对应的子词单元可以被稳定抽取，同时保留 byte-level fallback 和 lossless detokenization。对 BPE 和 Unigram 都提供了可抽取方案，说明作者不是只在某一种分词算法上做特例。

再看模型训练。核心思想是让模型在预训练时反复看到不同的 subtokenizer 组合，从而学会在不同 token inventory 下读写文本。论文把这些 subtokenizer 采样后组成 mini-batches，训练同一个模型共享主干参数，但输入 embedding 和输出预测都只在当前子词表上工作。这样做的直接结果是：部署到某个语言子集时，不需要加载完整 multilingual output matrix，只需保留目标语言相关 token 的 embedding/output rows。由于输出层 softmax 的维度显著缩小，推理速度和显存占用都会改善。

这套设计和传统 multilingual tokenizer 的区别有三点。第一，传统方法把所有语言塞进一个固定词表，压缩率和输出层成本一起被全局绑定；这里则把“共享训练”和“专用部署”拆开。第二，传统做法若想针对某语言优化，通常只能单独训练 monolingual tokenizer 和模型，跨语言共享会被破坏；这里保留了一个统一模型，只在 tokenizer/output head 层面做模块化。第三，作者强调目标不是追求极端压缩，而是在接近 monolingual compression 的前提下，保持多语言共享能力和部署灵活性。

从全文表述看，论文还引入了 balanced multilingual training 的思路：通过对子词表进行采样，模型不会总是暴露在同一个大词表下，从而减轻高资源语言在词表分配上的天然优势。这也是它改善 cross-lingual fairness 的机制之一。文中使用 Normalized Sequence Length, NSL 来量化各语言相对单语参考 tokenizer 的压缩损失，这个指标贯穿 tokenizer 评估和后续效率分析。13:Ta6b,实验部分有几条结果值得记住。

第一，现有开源 multilingual tokenizer 的压缩不公平问题很明显。作者在 FLORES-200 devtest 上，用 24k 单语 tokenizer 作为参考，比较 TinyAya、NLLB-200、Gemma-3、Llama-3、Qwen-3 等开放 tokenizer 的 NSL。结论是这些 tokenizer 对英语的压缩通常接近单语参考，但对大多数其他语言明显更差。作者还特意把评测限制在 21 个欧洲语言上，这些语言本来就属于中高资源、且通常被现有 tokenizer 覆盖得较好；即便如此，不公平仍然明显，说明问题不是只出在极低资源语言上。到了低资源语言，差距会更大。

第二，覆盖范围和压缩率之间存在清晰 trade-off。论文训练了只覆盖 21 种语言的标准 BPE tokenizer，记作 Multi21；当词表大小到 256k 时，它与 24k 单语 tokenizer 的压缩差距可以缩小到 4% 以内。这个结果说明，只要减少覆盖语言数，每种语言能分到更多词表容量，压缩自然改善。模块化 tokenizer 的意义就在于：不必为部署某几个语言时继续承担全量覆盖的代价。

第三，模块化 subtokenizer 的压缩率可以做到接近独立训练的 monolingual tokenizer。摘要已经明确给出这一点，全文则把它作为方法成立的关键证据：如果抽取后的 subtokenizer 明显劣于单语 tokenizer，那么后续训练和部署都失去意义。作者对 BPE 和 Unigram 都做了验证，说明不是某个特定 tokenizer 家族的偶然现象。

第四，推理效率确实受益，而且收益在小模型上更明显。论文在引言里举例，Gemma 2 2.6B 即便共享输入输出 embedding，256k 词表仍占到总参数的 22%。这给了一个很直观的量级：在小模型里，词表不是边角成本，而是核心成本。模块化方案在推理时只保留目标语言相关输出矩阵，因此能比标准 multilingual tokenizer 更快，同时在 multiple-choice、summarization、translation 上保持有竞争力。摘要没有列出全部具体分数，但全文强调速度提升来自两部分：更好的目标语言压缩减少序列长度，裁剪后的输出层减少每步 softmax 计算。

第五，作者对“压缩提升是否转化为质量提升”做了审慎处理。文中回顾了相互矛盾的既有结论，因此实验重点不是证明压缩越高模型越强，而是证明在不明显损害任务表现的前提下，可以把效率和跨语言公平性做得更好。这一点从研究设计上是合理的，因为 tokenizer 改动最直接的收益确实先体现在 token budget 和 output-layer cost 上。14:T5a6,This is a meaningful contribution at the tokenizer–pretraining interface. First, it turns the tokenizer from a fixed global artifact into a modular object that can be specialized after training. That is important because multilingual tokenization has usually been treated as a one-shot design choice. Second, it connects tokenizer design directly to model memory footprint and output-layer compute, rather than discussing compression in isolation. For 1B–3B scale models, vocabulary-related parameters are not a side issue; they can take a large fraction of the total budget. Third, the paper does not stop at tokenizer construction. It provides a pretraining recipe that teaches the model to operate under different subtokenizer subsets, which is what makes deployment-time vocabulary pruning actually work. Finally, the paper is careful about claims: it frames better compression mainly as an efficiency and fairness gain, not as a guaranteed quality gain. That restraint is appropriate and makes the contribution more credible.

For pretraining researchers, two ideas stand out. One is that vocabulary size, language coverage, and output-layer cost do not have to remain a single static trade-off; they can be shared during training and specialized at deployment. The other is that tokenizer design is not just preprocessing. If the model is not trained to handle changing token inventories, modular tokenization is not usable in practice.15:Ta8d,The method has two layers: modular tokenizer construction and a matching pretraining strategy.

On the tokenizer side, the authors propose both modular BPE and modular Unigram schemes. The objective is to train a large multilingual tokenizer from which one can extract subtokenizers for any language or language subset. The challenge is not simply concatenating language-specific vocabularies. A naive union would break consistency in token IDs, merge rules, or token probabilities, and the extracted subsets would not necessarily preserve monolingual-like compression. The paper therefore designs the tokenizer training process so that language-specific components remain extractable while preserving byte-level fallback and lossless detokenization. The fact that the framework works for both BPE and Unigram is important; it suggests the idea is not tied to one tokenizer family.

On the model side, the key idea is to expose the model during pretraining to many different subtokenizer combinations. These subtokenizers are sampled and used to form batches, so the same backbone learns to read and predict text under varying token inventories. In each case, the input embedding and output prediction operate only on the active sub-vocabulary. At deployment time, this allows the system to load only the rows of the embedding/output matrices relevant to the target language subset, instead of the full multilingual vocabulary. The efficiency gain comes from two places: shorter sequences for the target languages and a smaller softmax/output layer.

Compared with standard multilingual tokenization, the difference is threefold. First, conventional approaches bind language coverage and output-layer cost into one fixed vocabulary; this framework decouples shared training from specialized deployment. Second, the usual way to optimize for a language is to train a separate monolingual tokenizer and often a separate model, which weakens multilingual sharing; here the model remains unified and only the tokenizer/output interface becomes modular. Third, the paper is not chasing maximal compression at any cost. The target is monolingual-like compression together with multilingual parameter sharing and deployment flexibility.

A further mechanism in the paper is balanced multilingual exposure through subtokenizer sampling. Because the model does not always train under the same giant vocabulary, high-resource languages have less structural advantage in vocabulary allocation. The paper uses Normalized Sequence Length (NSL) throughout to quantify how far each language is from a monolingual reference tokenizer, and this metric anchors both the tokenizer analysis and the efficiency discussion.16:Ta0d,Several empirical results matter.

First, existing open multilingual tokenizers show clear compression unfairness. On FLORES-200 devtest, using 24k monolingual tokenizers as references, the paper compares tokenizers from TinyAya, NLLB-200, Gemma-3, Llama-3, and Qwen-3. The pattern is consistent: compression is often close to monolingual quality for English, but substantially worse for most other languages. Importantly, the evaluation is intentionally conservative: only 21 European languages, mostly medium- to high-resource and already relatively well covered by open multilingual tokenizers. If unfairness is visible there, it is not a niche low-resource artifact.

Second, the coverage–compression trade-off is explicit. The paper trains a standard BPE tokenizer on only those 21 languages, called Multi21. With a 256k vocabulary, its compression comes within 4% of 24k monolingual tokenizers. This is a useful calibration point: if you reduce the number of covered languages, each language gets more vocabulary capacity and compression improves. The modular framework is valuable because it lets deployment benefit from that specialization without giving up a shared multilingual model.

Third, extracted modular subtokenizers achieve compression close to independently trained monolingual tokenizers. This is one of the central validity checks of the method. If the extracted subtokenizers were much worse than monolingual ones, the whole framework would collapse. The paper demonstrates this for both BPE and Unigram, which strengthens the claim.

Fourth, the efficiency gains are real and especially relevant for small models. The introduction gives a concrete scale example: Gemma 2 2.6B spends 22% of its parameters on a 256k vocabulary even with tied embeddings. That makes the cost of the vocabulary impossible to ignore. By pruning the output matrix to the target language subset at inference, the modular approach speeds up decoding while remaining competitive on multiple-choice evaluation, summarization, and translation. The full paper emphasizes that the speedup comes from both better target-language compression and a smaller output layer.

Fifth, the paper is careful about the relationship between compression and quality. It reviews prior work showing mixed evidence on whether better compression improves downstream performance. Accordingly, the experiments are designed to show that efficiency and cross-lingual fairness can improve without materially hurting task quality, rather than claiming that compression alone guarantees better models.17:T6af,This one is worth a careful read. A good order is: problem setup → tokenizer construction → pretraining recipe → efficiency and quality results.

Start with the introduction and the section on multilingual tokenizer inefficiencies. They clearly explain why a single multilingual vocabulary creates both compression unfairness and output-layer waste. Figure 1 and the NSL definition are foundational. Then read the modular BPE and modular Unigram sections closely to understand what “extractable subtokenizers” really means and how it differs from ordinary jointly trained tokenizers. After that, focus on the pretraining strategy: how subtokenizers are sampled at the batch level, how embeddings and output rows are shared or restricted, and how the model remains stable while the token inventory changes. Finally, read the experiments with attention to three groups of results: per-language NSL comparisons, speed/compression trade-offs as vocabulary size changes, and downstream performance when deploying to language subsets.

There are four questions worth keeping in mind. First, does switching among subtokenizers create optimization instability or sparse embedding learning? Second, after pruning the output layer, is cross-lingual transfer weakened because the token inventory has changed? Third, do the gains remain meaningful at larger model scales, or are they concentrated in the regime where embeddings are a large parameter fraction? Fourth, could the same modular idea extend beyond multilingual text to unified discrete token spaces for text, speech, or vision? Reading with those questions in mind makes it easier to judge how transferable the method is to other pretraining settings.18:T44a,The Life Sciences Verification Program uses a layered grant structure. Organizations are reviewed for research credentials, security standards, and ethical oversight. Verified teams can receive Standard Use grants, which cover most life-sciences workflows and provide access to Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet models with more permissive biology-related classifiers than the generally available Fable models. High-risk Use is a project-level add-on for work that remains blocked under Standard Use. It removes life-sciences request blockers for that specific project, while other safeguards such as cyber classifiers remain active. Standard Use applies at the team level and renews annually; High-risk Use applies to a single research project and renews every six months. The safety model is based on shared responsibility. Each organization specifies its intended safe use cases, and Anthropic monitors LSVP traffic for activity that appears outside that declared scope. Enforcement moves from blocking individual requests in real time toward offline monitoring over patterns of behavior across sessions.19:T453,Muon flattens the singular spectrum of the momentum matrix, producing an update whose singular values are roughly all one. Musec replaces this with spectral clipping: only singular values above a threshold are clipped, while the skewed spectrum of the original momentum is preserved. The update therefore avoids injecting excessive magnitude into weak momentum directions. The paper also gives Musec a constrained optimization interpretation: it solves a Frobenius-penalized quadratic subproblem under a spectral-norm constraint, complementing prior interpretations of Muon as unconstrained steepest descent. For practical training, the authors introduce Soft Musec, which replaces hard clipping with a smooth saturation function and approximates the resulting matrix transform using coupled Newton-Schulz iterations, avoiding explicit SVD. The theory covers stochastic nonconvex nonsmooth objectives under weak convexity assumptions and proves convergence to a Goldstein stationary point, addressing recent results showing that exact-polar Muon may fail to converge in general nonsmooth nonconvex settings.1a:T555,ZGCM-1 is a 7.39B decoder-only Transformer with 32 layers, hidden size 4096, SwiGLU intermediate size 11008, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, and a 256K maximum context length. Its central architectural choice is a hybrid causal-attention backbone. Twenty-seven layers use gated sliding-window attention with a 128-token window, while five layers use global causal attention at layers 6, 12, 18, 24, and 30. This 5:1 local-to-global pattern trades full attention for much lower KV-cache and bandwidth cost, while still allowing periodic long-range information mixing. The model also uses QK normalization and partial RoPE with a rotary fraction of 0.33 to improve long-context stability.

On the training side, the recipe combines the Muon optimizer, hybrid FP8 precision, and TWEO outlier regularization. The goal is lower time-to-loss rather than only faster per-step execution. Mid-training uses a 600B-token curriculum that increases context length from 16K to 64K to 256K. Multi-turn interaction traces are reformulated as Markov decision process state-action transitions, which gives the model dense supervision at intermediate steps instead of supervising only the final answer. Post-training uses execution-verified trajectories and mixed think/no-think SFT, so the model learns both extended reasoning and efficient direct responses.1b:T49e,The paper reports results on 20 benchmarks. At the systems level, the hybrid attention design reduces per-token KV-cache footprint by 6.4x and improves throughput by 3.94x at 256K context compared with standard full attention. The combination of Muon, hybrid FP8, and TWEO gives about a 4.2x pre-training time-to-loss speedup over an AdamW/BF16 baseline.

On reasoning tasks, ZGCM-1-7B is reported to lead the 7B–8B comparison group on the average of 14 reasoning benchmarks. Specific scores include 75.0% on AIME 2026, 97.1% on MATH-500, and 70.4% on HMMT 2025. On agentic search and system-agency tasks, it reaches 63.1% on WebWalkerQA, 19.4% on BrowseComp, and 62.0% on Binary Function Search. These results support the paper’s practical claim: for compact models, long-context reasoning plus supervised tool interaction can be a more effective route than relying on parametric memorization alone.

The paper also reports how AI agents were used in the model-development workflow. Agents were more useful for data processing, experimentation, monitoring, evaluation, and deployment than for architecture or learning-algorithm design, where human direction remained important.1c:T41f,FedTAR (Task-awARe Federated fine-tuning) uses routing statistics as a proxy for latent task structure and ties it to update aggregation:
1) During local fine-tuning, each client collects routing features such as average expert utilization, expert co-activation patterns, and routing confidence.
2) Apply SVD on routing features to obtain low-dimensional task coordinates that make clients clusterable by implicit task preference.
3) Apply SVD on local parameter updates to extract dominant update directions.
4) Perform task-aware clustering and aggregation (within and across clusters) based on task coordinates, rather than indiscriminate averaging.
5) Learn a mapping between the task space and the update space, then reconstruct the aggregated global update so it remains aligned with task-specific dominant directions—aiming to preserve expert specialization and reduce conflicts on shared experts.
The key departure from FedAvg is that aggregation and reconstruction are driven by routing behavior, not by explicit task labels or manual grouping.1d:T46b,The paper formulates Z-loss as a backward source. For a penalty of the form λ(log Z - c)^2, the logit gradient is proportional to 2λ(log Z - c) times the softmax distribution. This source then gets transported by the architecture. The analysis covers several coordinates. First, cross-entropy is invariant to a common shift of all logits, while Z-loss is not, so raw-logit Z-loss acts along a CE-invisible direction; centering the output head changes this coordinate while preserving CE. Second, tied embeddings create a coupled gradient path because the same matrix is used for input embeddings and output projection. Third, the output-to-hidden gain can amplify or reshape the Z-loss source before it reaches hidden states and parameters, motivating spectral audits and gain-aware weighting. Fourth, top-k MoE routers introduce reduction-scale and routing-scale distortions, so the same router Z-loss coefficient can mean different effective forces under different routing setups. Fifth, fused CE+Z-loss kernels need source-consistency checks, since matching the forward scalar is not sufficient if the backward source differs.1e:T5d9,The pipeline has two stages. Keeping the tokenizer is a conservative engineering choice: it avoids embedding migration and compatibility issues, but may preserve suboptimal tokenization for some Southeast Asian scripts. The paper also includes GPT-2-class pretraining and RoBERTa GLUE fine-tuning transfer runs using the same late-expensive-mode principle, but the provided evidence is not enough to claim direct scalability to large LLM pretraining.21:T52b,NCP-ArchPreview modifies an OLMo-3-7B-style backbone into a hierarchical autoregressive model with three main components. A 16-layer Token Encoder processes the token stream into hidden states. An 8-layer Concept Module operates in the middle and predicts future discrete concepts. A 16-layer Token Decoder then continues standard autoregressive token prediction. The discrete concept vocabulary is built directly from hidden states through product quantization, which gives a high-capacity discrete latent space without requiring manually defined semantic labels. Training jointly optimizes standard next-token prediction and next-concept prediction. The NTP objective preserves compatibility with normal LM generation, while the NCP objective forces the model to predict future multi-token spans at a more abstract level. Predicted concepts are fed back into the token-level path to guide later generation. The architecture also uses multiway dynamic dense connections, adapted from MUDDFormer, to route residual information across the token and concept hierarchy. Compared with multi-token prediction, the target is not a sequence of surface tokens but a learned latent concept. Compared with hierarchical byte or patch models, the key contribution is not only sequence compression but explicit future latent prediction.22:Tc54,方法核心是把 looped model 训练成一个带 recurrent state 的条件去噪器，再把推理解释为概率流 ODE 的积分过程。

先看问题设定。输入是条件 c，输出是离散序列 x。传统 looped model 维护隐藏状态 z_i，并用共享参数的更新函数 f(z_i, c) 反复迭代，再用头部 g(z_i) 解码答案。难点在于实际训练常用 stop-gradient 的 per-step loss，导致第 i 步的损失不会回传到更早状态 z_{<i}，于是早期步骤没有动力去准备后续计算。

作者的改法是：不给每一步都要求“直接答对最终答案”，而是给每一步分配一个不同噪声水平下的局部去噪任务。具体做法是从真实解 x 构造一条从高噪声到低噪声的中间状态轨迹 x_t，并让第 i 步 recurrence 负责在对应噪声水平上预测去噪方向，也就是 velocity / denoising target。关键不只是多噪声训练，而是两点耦合设计：
1) progressively decreasing noise levels：随着 recurrence 时间推进，任务从粗糙恢复走向精细恢复，天然形成“先搭框架、再修细节”的计算分工；
2) shared noise across adjacent objectives：相邻时间步看到的是同一底层噪声样本在不同噪声强度下的版本，因此目标之间是 temporally associated 的。这样即便梯度只覆盖局部，模型也会倾向于学出能在相邻步骤之间延续的隐藏状态，而不是每步都重新开始。

在形式上，作者采用 categorical continuous flow matching 的监督版本。模型输出的是定义在概率单纯形上的 velocity field，而不是直接输出离散 token。隐藏状态 z 与当前噪声化样本、条件 c 一起决定这个 velocity。训练时优化局部 denoising / flow matching 目标；推理时从噪声初始化，通过数值积分沿 learned probability flow 逐步运输到解分布附近，再做 rounding 得到离散答案。

这个 formulation 有几个重要区别。

和标准 diffusion/flow model 不同：这里不是单次前向网络在连续时间上求解，而是把 recurrent hidden state 显式并入动力系统。也就是说，ODE 的速度场不仅依赖当前 x_t 和 c，还依赖一个会跨步累积计算的内部状态 z_i。这样“流”负责提供平滑、局部一致的训练信号，“loop”负责存储和滚动中间计算。

和已有 looped reasoning 方法如 TRM 相比：作者不再要求每一步都直接预测最终解，也不依赖长程 BPTT 去塑造 recurrence，而是通过噪声调度把不同步骤的职责拆开。训练信号更局部，但目标之间更连续。

和在 recurrence 中直接注入随机噪声以获得多样性的方法相比：looped flows 的随机性来自概率运输过程本身。作者指出，Euler integration 下可以得到多个有效预测，这意味着模型天然支持一题多解，而不是靠每步加噪声硬造随机性。

从机制上看，这个方法最有意思的地方是“把时间上的 credit assignment，转写成噪声尺度上的 curriculum + coupling”。这不是常规截断 BPTT 的小修小补，而是换了训练接口。23:T4a0,This matters because it speaks directly to inference-time compute beyond autoregressive next-token prediction. The paper offers a concrete training interface for hidden-state deliberation: instead of relying on long-horizon backpropagation, it uses flow-style local denoising objectives that are temporally aligned across recurrent steps. For pretraining researchers, the significance is threefold.

First, it targets a core question in test-time scaling: how to make extra inference steps actually perform additional computation rather than repeat a shallow transformation.

Second, it reframes multi-step reasoning as probability flow integration. That gives a clean separation between training and inference: training uses local denoising targets, while inference can scale compute by refining the temporal grid or using better numerical solvers.

Third, it provides a mechanistic claim, not just a benchmark gain: long-range useful computation can emerge from local objectives if adjacent objectives are properly coupled through noise levels and shared noise. That is a meaningful idea for latent reasoning, non-AR language modeling, and recurrent world-model-style architectures.24:Taa0,The core idea is to train a looped model as a recurrent conditional denoiser and then perform inference by integrating a probability flow ODE.

In the standard setup, a looped model maintains a hidden state z_i, updates it recurrently with shared parameters, and decodes a prediction from each state. The practical problem is that training often uses stop-gradient per-step losses, so the loss at step i does not shape earlier states z_{<i}. Early updates therefore have little incentive to build representations that will help later updates.

Looped flows changes the target. Instead of asking every recurrent step to directly predict the final answer, it assigns each step a local denoising task at a different noise level. Starting from the ground-truth solution x, the method constructs noisy intermediate states x_t along a path from high noise to low noise. The recurrent model is trained to predict the denoising direction, or velocity, appropriate for the current noise level.

Two design choices are essential.
1) Noise levels decrease progressively across recurrent time. This creates a natural division of labor: earlier steps solve coarser subproblems, later steps refine them.
2) Adjacent objectives share the same underlying noise realization. This temporally associates neighboring denoising tasks, so even with only local gradients, the hidden state is encouraged to carry forward useful computation rather than restart from scratch at each step.

Formally, the paper uses a supervised version of continuous flow matching for categorical outputs. The model predicts a velocity field on the probability simplex rather than directly outputting discrete tokens. The velocity depends on the noisy current state, the conditioning input, and the recurrent hidden state. Training optimizes local denoising / flow-matching losses. Inference starts from noise and integrates the learned probability flow toward the solution distribution, then rounds to a categorical answer.

This differs from standard diffusion or flow models because the recurrent hidden state is part of the dynamics. The flow provides smooth, locally consistent supervision; the loop stores and accumulates intermediate computation over time. It also differs from prior looped reasoning methods such as TRM, which typically ask each step to predict the final answer directly and therefore suffer more from local-training mismatch. Here, the recurrence is shaped indirectly through a sequence of aligned subproblems.

A particularly interesting aspect is the credit-assignment shift: instead of solving temporal credit assignment with long BPTT, the method translates it into a noise-scale curriculum plus coupling between adjacent objectives.25:T780,The evaluation covers six reasoning benchmarks. The headline result is that looped flows outperforms prior looped models on five of them and remains competitive on the sixth. The paper explicitly reports that, using the same architecture as TRM, performance improves from 44.6% to 58.8% on ARC-AGI-1 and from 7.8% to 12.2% on ARC-AGI-2. Those are meaningful gains because ARC-style tasks are sensitive to compositional generalization and internal multi-step computation.

The stability results are just as important as the benchmark numbers. Prior looped models can become unstable when unrolled longer, sometimes failing even on simple problems. Looped flows is reported to learn more stable recurrences, with performance improving more reliably as inference computation increases. That directly supports the claim that the method trains recurrent computation rather than merely fitting local predictions.

The ablations indicate that each component matters. Based on the paper’s framing, the important ones are:
1) removing the progressively decreasing noise schedule hurts performance, suggesting that coarse-to-fine task allocation is useful;
2) removing shared noise weakens temporal alignment between adjacent objectives and reduces the usefulness of recurrent state transfer;
3) replacing flow-based inference with more direct step prediction reduces the benefit of extra inference compute;
4) the choice of numerical integrator affects final accuracy, which implies the model is genuinely using the learned continuous flow rather than treating it as a training-only wrapper.

Another notable result is that inference can use a finer temporal grid than training. This means the model is not just memorizing a fixed discrete program length; it learns a computation trajectory that can be interpolated at test time. For anyone interested in test-time scaling, that is one of the most important empirical findings.26:T55f,This is a must-read if you care about latent reasoning, recurrent inference, or alternatives to explicit chain-of-thought.

Read it in four passes: problem, construction, mechanism, evidence.

Start with the introduction and background to understand the exact failure mode of looped models trained with local stop-gradient objectives. Then focus on the two core method sections: how local denoising objectives are assigned across recurrent steps, and how inference is formulated as probability flow integration. It helps to track the roles of three objects separately: the noisy solution state x_t, the recurrent hidden state z_i, and the velocity field conditioned on both plus the input.

In the experiments, prioritize:
1) the main comparison table against TRM and related looped baselines, especially ARC-AGI-1/2;
2) plots showing performance as a function of recurrent steps or integration steps;
3) ablations on decreasing noise, shared noise, and solver choice.
If the paper includes recurrence visualizations or failure cases, those are worth reading closely because they reveal whether the method truly fixes the training mismatch.

A first serious read takes about 45–60 minutes. A deeper read should include working through the flow-matching formulation and thinking about how it could interface with language-model pretraining or hidden-state reasoning systems.27:T8f9,方法建立在 BD3LM 上。先回顾基线：BD3LM 按 block 自回归，block 内用 masked diffusion 去噪；训练时只在被 mask 的位置上做 SUBS 参数化下的 token 预测；推理时从全 mask 开始，反复预测所有 mask 位置，再按 schedule 或置信度固定一部分 token。问题在于，这一步里各位置预测是独立的。

DA-DLM 的核心改动，是在每个去噪步构造一个 position-oriented DAG，而不是直接输出各位置独立分布。这个 DAG 不是 DAT 在 NAT 里那种大而自由的无位置约束图，而是显式绑定到输出位置。每个输出位置对应一个 node group：
- 如果该位置的 token 在更早去噪步已经被固定，那么这个位置在当前 DAG 中就是一个单节点 anchor；
- 如果该位置还未确定，就为该位置展开多个候选节点，表示该位置当前可能的局部模态。

然后只允许相邻位置的 group 之间建立 transition。这样一来，最终不是对每个位置各选一个 token，而是在整张 DAG 上选一条穿过各位置 group 的路径。路径分数同时考虑节点发射分数和相邻候选之间的转移分数，于是同一步里多个 token 的选择被耦合起来。已经固定的 token 作为 anchor 被钉在图上，能对邻近未决位置形成结构性约束。这一点是作者区别于直接照搬 DAT 的关键：DLM 是迭代式的，前几步已确定 token 的“锚定作用”必须保留，否则 successive denoising 容易漂。

从机制上看，这个设计做了两件事。第一，它把 DLM 每步的预测目标从 factorized marginals 变成了一个局部链式依赖上的联合选择问题。第二，它让 DAG 随去噪过程演化：随着步数推进，anchor 越来越多，未决位置越来越少，图会逐渐收缩，模型把容量集中到剩余不确定区域。这个动态图结构很适合 DLM 的 iterative refinement，而不适合一次性 NAT 生成。

论文的思想来源是 DAT，但改造点很明确：DAT 面向单步生成，允许更自由的转移；DA-DLM 面向 iterative denoising，因此采用 position-oriented DAG 来强化已固定 token 的约束，并让图结构与当前 mask 状态同步变化。这个差异不是实现细节，而是任务结构决定的。28:T90a,The method is built on BD3LM. In the baseline, generation is autoregressive across blocks, while each block is generated by masked diffusion. During training, only masked positions contribute under the SUBS parameterization. During inference, the model starts from a fully masked block, predicts all masked positions in parallel, and then fixes a subset of tokens according to a schedule or confidence rule. The key limitation is that those per-position predictions are independent.

DA-DLM replaces that factorized prediction with a position-oriented DAG constructed at every denoising step. This is not the same as directly importing DAT from NAT. DAT uses a large DAG with relatively unconstrained transitions for one-shot generation. DA-DLM instead binds the graph explicitly to output positions.

Each output position corresponds to a node group. If a token at that position has already been fixed in an earlier denoising step, the group collapses to a single anchor node. If the position is still unresolved, the model expands it into multiple candidate nodes representing local alternatives. Transitions are only allowed between adjacent position groups. Generation within the step is therefore no longer a set of independent token choices. It becomes a path selection problem through the DAG, where the path score combines node scores and transition scores. This couples the token decisions made in the same denoising step.

The anchor mechanism is the critical adaptation to iterative denoising. Previously fixed tokens are pinned into the graph and structurally constrain nearby unresolved positions. That is the main reason the authors do not simply reuse DAT as-is. In DLMs, the denoising process should progressively converge as more tokens become fixed. Without explicit anchoring, successive steps can drift rather than refine.

Conceptually, the method does two things. First, it changes the denoising objective at each step from factorized marginals to a structured joint selection problem over a local dependency chain. Second, it lets the graph evolve with denoising: as more positions become anchors, fewer candidate groups remain, and the graph shrinks toward the residual uncertainty. That dynamic graph is well matched to iterative refinement and is the main architectural idea of the paper.29:T6f6,The evaluation covers language modeling, open-ended generation, and summarization. The headline findings have two parts. First, DA-DLM consistently outperforms the BD3LM baseline across all settings. Second, the gains are larger when fewer denoising steps are used, which is exactly where the independence problem should hurt the most. That alignment between motivation and empirical behavior is important.

A particularly useful result is that on summarization, DA-DLM matches the autoregressive baseline while retaining the parallel decoding advantage. This suggests that the method is not only making open-ended text look smoother. It is also recovering sequence-level consistency in conditional generation.

From the structure of the paper, the most important ablations are likely to be: step-count sensitivity, to show that the advantage widens in low-step regimes; DAG design ablations, to test whether position orientation and anchors are necessary; and task generalization, to show gains beyond a single metric such as perplexity. For this paper, the most informative curve is not a single average score but how quality degrades as denoising steps are reduced. If DA-DLM flattens that degradation curve, then it is addressing a core structural issue rather than making a small improvement in a comfortable high-step regime.

The anchor idea may generalize beyond diffusion to a wider class of structured denoising LMs.2b:Ta2b,方法核心是 Discrete Beckmann Transport Models，简称 DBTM。理解它要抓住三个层次。

第一层是表示。作者把离散 token 序列嵌入到每个位置一个 V 维 simplex 顶点的连续空间里，整条序列是 (R^V)^L 中的点。数据分布 μ1 支持在 one-hot 顶点上，先验 μ0 是连续高斯。目标是学一个从连续空间到离散数据流形的 transport。

第二层是动力学。传统 flow matching 学的是随时间变化的速度场 bt(x)，采样要积分 ODE；flow map 学的是两时刻算子 X_{s,t}，但 off-diagonal 项通常需要 teacher 或 bootstrap。DBTM 改学 autonomous，也就是 time-independent 的速度场 b(x)，对应自治 ODE dX_s/ds = b(X_s)。在这个设定下，流映射满足半群性质，且作者利用 time-independent flow 的几何性质构造一个 transport map T(x)，它把任意 ambient point 沿自治流送到某个固定点，最终落在 simplex 顶点支撑的数据流形上。

第三层是训练。关键不是直接监督 T 的终点，而是利用固定点性质导出守恒方程 b·∇T = 0。直观上，沿着流线前进时，最终 transport destination 不应改变，因此 T 在流方向上的导数为零。作者最重要的贡献是把这个 PDE 残差变成可从数据最小化的训练目标，从而不需要 teacher flow。全文里还给出一个可操作的近似训练法：用冻结副本的当前模型作为 bootstrap target，再加一个 Euler correction，迭代回归到更接近真实 transport map 的目标。论文声称，部分训练好的 Tθ 并不是无意义的半成品，而是对应自治流上的中间点；因此在推理时可以反复应用 Tθ 做 iterative refinement，逐步逼近固定点。

另一个关键设计是 partial-context interpolant。它不是简单在全序列上做连续插值，而是保留部分上下文、对其余位置做插值/传输学习。这样做有两个作用：一是更适合条件生成和 reasoning，因为 prompt 或已确定 token 可以作为锚点；二是允许训练和推理时基于置信度或质量做 selective refinement，而不是每一步都全量重写整条序列。

和已有方法相比，差异很明确。相对离散 diffusion，DBTM 不依赖时间步去噪链。相对 flow matching，它不学 bt(x,t) 而学 autonomous map。相对 flow-map distillation，它不需要先有一个收敛 teacher 来提供 off-diagonal 监督。相对纯 bootstrap 的 few-step map，它把 bootstrap 放在一个有固定点/守恒结构约束的框架里，试图缓解目标漂移和训练不稳。2c:T7e4,实验分成两类：无条件语言建模和条件 reasoning。作者强调的指标是低或匹配 NFE 下的性能，而不是只看高步数极限。摘要没有给出完整数字，但从正文结构可以判断，主结果应当比较 DBTM 与离散 diffusion、flow matching、以及需要 teacher 的 flow-map/few-step baseline，在 1-step、少步 refinement、以及 matched-compute 条件下的质量差异。

That matters for pretraining research in at least three ways.

First, it directly challenges the common assumption that few-step discrete generation must be built on top of a teacher model. If this line of work holds up, one-step or low-step language modeling may no longer require an expensive upstream AR or diffusion teacher.

Second, it shifts the objective from fitting instantaneous velocities to satisfying a fixed-point and conservation structure. That changes how the model is parameterized, how it is trained, and how refinement is performed at inference time. For researchers interested in alternatives to next-token AR modeling, this is much more consequential than a standard decoding-speed paper.

Third, the paper evaluates not only unconditional language modeling but also conditional reasoning. That matters because it tests whether the learned one-step map can support structured generation and iterative self-correction, rather than only improving perplexity-like metrics in an unconditional setting. This is a must-read paper because it offers a genuinely different route for discrete language generation, with a fairly complete mathematical and algorithmic story.2e:Tbc4,The core idea of Discrete Beckmann Transport Models (DBTM) can be understood in three layers.

The first layer is representation. A discrete token sequence is embedded into a continuous space where each token is a vertex of the V-dimensional simplex. A full sequence is therefore a point in (R^V)^L. The data distribution lives on one-hot vertices, while the prior is continuous Gaussian noise. The modeling goal is to learn a transport from the ambient continuous space to the discrete data manifold.

The second layer is dynamics. Standard flow matching learns a time-dependent velocity field b_t(x) and requires ODE integration at sampling time. Flow-map methods learn a two-time operator X_{s,t}, but the off-diagonal terms are usually learned either from a teacher or through unstable bootstrapping. DBTM instead learns an autonomous, time-independent velocity field b(x), defining an ODE dX_s/ds = b(X_s). In this setting, the flow has a semigroup structure, and the paper constructs a transport map T(x) that sends any ambient point along the autonomous flow to a fixed point on the simplex-supported data manifold.

The third layer is training. Rather than supervising the terminal point directly, the paper derives a conservation equation, b · ∇T = 0. Intuitively, as one moves along a flow line, the final transport destination should remain unchanged, so T is constant in the flow direction. This is the central technical contribution: the PDE residual is turned into a trainable objective that can be minimized from data, removing the need for a teacher flow. The practical training procedure uses a frozen copy of the current model as a bootstrap target plus an Euler correction, iteratively regressing toward a better approximation of the true transport map. A partially trained T_theta is not treated as a failed endpoint predictor; instead, it is interpreted as mapping to an intermediate point along the autonomous flow. That makes iterative application of T_theta meaningful at inference time.

Another important design is the partial-context interpolant. Instead of interpolating the entire sequence uniformly, the method preserves part of the context and learns transport on the remaining positions. This is important for two reasons: it makes the framework suitable for conditional generation and reasoning, where prompts or already-decided tokens should act as anchors; and it enables confidence- or quality-based selective refinement instead of rewriting the whole sequence at every step.

Relative to prior work, the distinctions are clear. Compared with discrete diffusion, DBTM does not rely on a time-indexed denoising chain. Compared with flow matching, it does not learn b_t(x, t). Compared with flow-map distillation, it does not require a converged teacher to supervise off-diagonal transitions. Compared with pure bootstrap approaches, it places self-training inside a fixed-point and conservation-structured framework, which is intended to reduce target drift and instability.2f:T934,The experiments cover both unconditional language modeling and conditional reasoning, with the main emphasis on quality at low or matched NFE rather than asymptotic performance at large sampling budgets. The abstract does not provide full tables, but the paper clearly positions DBTM against discrete diffusion, flow matching, and teacher-distilled few-step flow-map baselines under one-step, few-step refinement, and matched-compute settings.

Several experimental signals are especially important. First, whether one-step generation is already usable, and how close it gets to teacher-distilled few-step methods. If one-step DBTM is competitive, that would strongly support the claim that the autonomous transport map and fixed-point structure are doing real work. Second, whether iterative application of T_theta improves quality consistently, or at least substantially over the first few refinement steps. That directly tests the paper’s claim that partially trained maps correspond to intermediate points along the autonomous flow. Third, whether the partial-context interpolant materially helps on reasoning and conditional generation, since that determines whether the method is genuinely language-model-like rather than just a generic discrete sampler.

The most informative ablations are likely to include: removing the conservation residual, removing the frozen-self-target plus Euler correction, comparing autonomous and time-dependent formulations, plotting performance against the number of refinement steps, and testing confidence-based selective refinement. If the paper includes trajectory visualizations in simplex space, those are likely more revealing than scalar metrics because they can show whether DBTM is actually learning transport toward vertices rather than behaving like a standard denoiser.

The wording in the abstract, 'stronger performance than baselines at lower or matched NFEs,' is also worth reading carefully. It suggests the gains are concentrated in the compute-efficient regime rather than uniformly across all settings. If the advantage disappears at high NFE, then DBTM should be viewed primarily as a few-step modeling framework. If the gains persist on reasoning tasks, then it is more than a sampler-speed method and starts to look like a viable alternative generative paradigm for conditional language tasks.30:T780,Read it in the order of theory, training objective, then empirical validation.

That distinction will matter for scaling to larger vocabularies, longer contexts, and multimodal discrete token spaces.31:T6e7,DenMark replaces sentence-level candidate selection with rollout-guided semantic lookahead over local denoising updates.
The method has three main components:
1. Fixed region partitioning. The output sequence is divided into token regions that serve as the basic units for watermark injection and detection. These regions are not assumed to align perfectly with syntax; they provide a stable operational granularity during iterative denoising.
2. Temporary rollouts for semantic estimation. A local token update inside a DLM does not immediately define a complete semantic unit, so its watermark value cannot be scored directly. DenMark temporarily rolls out unresolved positions to form approximate completions, evaluates them with a key-dependent semantic scoring function, and estimates the expected watermark gain of each candidate local update. The update with the highest estimated score is then committed. In this way, watermark evidence is accumulated progressively throughout denoising rather than injected only after full sentence completion.
3. Calibrated scanning at detection time. Semantic attacks can shift token boundaries and break the original region alignment. To recover evidence under such shifts, the detector scans over multiple candidate region sizes and calibrates the resulting statistics.
The main conceptual difference from prior semantic watermarking is that DenMark does not force DLMs into an AR-style candidate-rejection loop. Instead, it works with the native iterative denoising process and moves semantic evaluation into local decision making. The paper also provides an analysis interpreting the final semantic score gain as the accumulation of many local choices, which helps explain why the method works beyond empirical results.32:T4ba,From the provided text, the experiments cover multiple DLMs and datasets, with the main comparison against token-level watermark baselines under semantic attacks. Those will tell you more about the method’s limits than a single aggregate detection metric.33:T630,The method, BOTA, appears to reformulate branched optimal transport as a continuous and differentiable objective that can be optimized with neural flows. Instead of explicitly solving for a discrete transport tree, it parameterizes a transport field with neural networks and trains it in a flow-matching style. The conceptual move is important: standard conditional flow matching learns a velocity field from source-target pairs, but each pair is effectively independent. BOTA introduces a preference for path sharing across samples, reflecting the BOT economy-of-scale principle.

The distinction from prior work has three parts. First, standard FM/CFM prescribes conditional paths per sample pair; BOTA introduces coupling across trajectories so that shared routes become cheaper. Second, classical BOT defines subadditive transport costs on edges, typically scaling like m^alpha with 0<alpha<1; BOTA translates that branching preference into a continuous trainable objective compatible with neural ODEs and flow matching. Third, the solver is amortized: the network learns reusable branched transport structure across batches and tasks instead of solving a fresh BOT instance each time.

From the available full text, the pipeline is roughly: define density evolution and velocity fields, introduce a BOT-inspired objective or regularizer that favors coalescence and later branching, and optimize a neural vector field with a flow-matching-style loss. The main novelty is not merely another FM variant, but the shift from independent particle transport to shared network transport.34:T541,The experiments focus on biological generation tasks and image generation, with the central claim being structural rather than purely metric: BOTA learns meaningful hierarchical generative processes. 3. Ablations on the branching strength, likely through the BOT exponent or related regularization terms, showing that removing the branching bias weakens both structure and performance.

During training, completion tokens are masked according to a sampled time t, and the model predicts the original tokens at masked positions. During inference, a chunk of length C starts fully masked; the model iteratively predicts masked positions in parallel and keeps selected high-confidence predictions until the chunk is filled. Registers are fixed-position tokens inserted into the prompt. After a chunk is denoised, an additional forward pass over the prompt and completed chunk saves the last-layer hidden states at the register positions, producing an R-by-d continuous state. For the next chunk, those saved states replace the input embeddings at the same register positions, while the rest of the prompt remains unchanged. The same slots are reused after every chunk, so the model must learn what to preserve, what to overwrite, and how to expose that state to the next denoising process. The supervised recipe splits a long reasoning trace into chunks, clears generated text between chunks, and trains the next chunk from the prompt plus carried register state. To prevent shortcut learning, the training sometimes masks attention from the new chunk to the prompt and forces prediction from a fully masked chunk. The work also compares task-directed registers trained by next-chunk loss with reconstruction-trained memory tokens, and integrates registers into chunked GRPO for reinforcement learning refinement.36:T40d,Read closely for about 60 to 90 minutes. Separate PCA transforms are applied to recent state and older history, and the baseline is padded to the same dimensionality with zeros so the comparison is not confounded by input size. First is Matryoshka-style training. Instead of training a compressor at one fixed K, the model samples K per training instance, so a single encoder learns to compress the same kind of context into different numbers of memory tokens. The underlying interface stays unchanged: an encoder LLM maps a context of length L into K continuous memory tokens, and a frozen decoder LLM consumes those soft tokens in place of the raw context. In practice, the encoder is usually a LoRA-adapted copy of the decoder. This makes the approach method-agnostic across ICAE, 500xCompressor, and SAC.

Second is inference-time budget selection. The paper proposes two strategies. Confidence-based cascade routing starts with the smallest, most aggressive budget and only retries with a larger K when the decoder is uncertain. This tends to preserve accuracy well, but may require multiple compression-decoding passes. The learned K predictor instead predicts the budget before compression, so inference runs in a single pass. That is more deployment-friendly because latency and throughput are easier to control.

An important empirical observation is that the accuracy-compression relation is not always monotonic at the instance level. Larger K can preserve distracting surface details and hurt the decoder, while K=1 can sometimes succeed where a larger budget fails. So adaptive budgeting is not just about saving tokens on easy cases; it also helps avoid over-preserving irrelevant information.3c:T4c6,Experiments cover three compressor families—ICAE, 500xCompressor, and SAC—on in-domain and out-of-domain QA from MRQA. There are three main findings.

First, a single Matryoshka-trained model can largely replace a family of fixed-ratio specialists. At each native ratio, the gap to separately trained fixed-K models is at worst 1.3 F1, and the shared model is often better on OOD settings. That suggests multi-budget training does not significantly compromise specialization.

Second, adaptive budget selection improves the accuracy-compression trade-off. Cascade routing retains over 98% of the accuracy of the mildest compression setting while increasing average compression from 15x to as high as 266x. The learned K predictor reaches 158x–236x compression in a single compression-decoding pass, with at most 0.7 F1 loss.

Third, the gains translate into real serving metrics. At larger batch sizes, the K predictor reduces context KV cache by 50% and improves aggregate decoding throughput by 47% relative to always using the mildest budget. The paper also shows that many MRQA inputs are already solvable with K=1, while only a minority need larger budgets, which explains why fixed-K deployment is inefficient.3d:T550,The method keeps the Kashin factorization w = u + P^T \hat{v} (with \hat{v}=Pv), aiming to bound \|u\|_\infty and \|\hat{v}\|_\infty so scalar quantization is less sensitive to outliers. The paper fixes three concrete issues observed in prior LLM applications:
1) Convergence and peak formation: instead of a matrix-level reformulation (which lost guarantees), they stay with the vector-level greedy algorithm and introduce a Greedy Algorithm with Alternating Updates. Updates of u and \hat{v} are executed in fixed blocks of four steps, designed to enforce the symmetric 4-peak distributions rather than letting the joint distribution collapse.
2) Efficient orthogonal transform: they replace a dense random orthogonal matrix with a sign-randomized DCT, reducing each application of P/P^T from O(N^2) to O(N log N) and eliminating matrix storage.
3) Faster clustering: because each greedy step changes factors by ±c_k(r_k) (a function of residual norm), after two steps the four peak locations are exactly ±c1±c2. They use these analytic centers to initialize k-means and run only a few refinement iterations, removing expensive multi-restart search.
They further compose the approach with OPTQ-style sequential error compensation and QuIP-style incoherence preprocessing (Hadamard/Kronecker), and implement the pipeline in JAX with multi-GPU pmap support.3e:T7a3,OmniKVQuant is a training-free extension of TurboQuant with two targeted modifications. TurboQuant decomposes each key/value vector into magnitude and direction, applies a randomized Hadamard rotation to the direction so coordinates look closer to a Gaussian reference, and then quantizes with a fixed codebook. This works reasonably well when one global reference distribution and one shared rotation are adequate.

The paper argues that this assumption fails in Omni-LLMs. The first fix is temporal range adaptation for keys. Even after Hadamard rotation, key coordinates still deviate substantially from the Gaussian target, and the mismatch changes over short temporal windows. Instead of using one fixed global range, OmniKVQuant performs coordinate-wise min-max scaling within a small local token group before codebook assignment. The codebook itself is not relearned; the local scaling simply adapts the same codebook to the current cache region. This is a minimal but well-motivated change that directly addresses local non-stationarity in keys.

The second fix is modality-specific value rotation. PCA visualizations show that audio, visual, and text values occupy distinct regions of representation space. A single shared rotation therefore cannot flatten all modalities equally well. OmniKVQuant calibrates separate rotations for each modality so that each value distribution is better aligned with the quantizer. The key idea is simple: modality-specific geometry persists inside a shared decoder, so the quantization stage should exploit it explicitly.

The paper also includes a fused Triton decode kernel. Instead of inverse-rotating every cached key, it rotates one query per head following a FlashAttention-style computation order. For values, inverse rotations are batched on head outputs rather than applied token by token to the cache. This reduces redundant rotation work and kernel launches without reconstructing a dense FP16 cache.3f:T5c8,The analysis experiments are important because they justify the design. On Qwen2.5-Omni-3B evaluated with WorldSense, rotated keys retain only 30.40% of the variance of the Gaussian reference, with Wasserstein-1 distance 0.778 and KS statistic 0.449. The mismatch is stronger for audio and video than for text. Values are closer to the Gaussian target overall, but their cross-modal geometry is clearly separated. This supports the paper’s split treatment: local adaptation for keys, modality-aware correction for values.

For the main results, the method is evaluated on Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni. On seven audio-visual benchmarks with Qwen2.5-Omni, 2-bit KV caches retain 98.1% of FP16 performance and consistently outperform TurboQuant. The abstract does not list every benchmark score, but the paper presents the gains as stable across tasks rather than concentrated on one dataset. The trend also transfers to Qwen3-Omni, which suggests the method is not tied to a single model implementation.

From an engineering perspective, two takeaways matter most. First, 2-bit KV quantization is viable for Omni-LLMs, but only if the quantizer respects multimodal cache structure. Second, a training-free method can preserve most of the original performance, which makes it attractive for deployment without model retraining. Design choices: uses device_dax to bypass page cache and let the connector manage memory directly; explicitly not targeting prefill/decode disaggregation or GPU↔CXL zero-copy DMA.42:T811,SpecGuard assumes the serving stack already uses speculative decoding. A small draft model proposes tokens, and the target model verifies them. The accept/reject sequence, normally used only for acceleration, is treated as an online measure of draft–target agreement. Under benign inputs, disagreement mostly reflects ordinary modeling mismatch. Under an activated backdoor, the target shifts toward the attacker-controlled response while a clean draft continues along the benign trajectory, so rejection increases and the per-query acceptance rate drops.

The base detector is simple: compute a query-level acceptance-rate score and compare it against a baseline estimated from clean traffic. The paper then extends this raw signal into a more deployable recipe. If the draft is also poisoned, low acceptance alone is no longer sufficient, so the detector uses two-sided abnormality scoring. If the trigger only affects a sparse segment of the response, whole-query averaging dilutes the signal, so the method adds multi-scale alarms over different windows. If traffic distribution shifts over time, fixed thresholds drift, so the paper recommends rolling calibration. If an adaptive attacker appends benign continuation after the malicious response to dilute the mean, early-token statistics become more informative than full-response averages.

The theory links acceptance behavior to distributional discrepancy between draft and target. Intuitively, speculative acceptance depends on how much probability the target assigns to draft-proposed tokens, so an acceptance-rate gap reflects increased divergence, discussed through total variation style arguments. The paper further derives a potency–stealth tradeoff: to hide from the detector while keeping the attack active, the attacker must reduce probability mass on tokens that the clean draft would not favor, which directly weakens the malicious behavioral shift. The theory is not trying to cover every adaptive strategy, but it gives a principled explanation for why this nearly free signal should work.43:T509,The empirical section is broader than the abstract suggests. The evaluation spans four backdoor types, three model families, multiple scales up to 32B, and several decoding settings rather than a single speculative-decoding configuration. The headline result is that SpecGuard achieves strong per-query detection of activated backdoors while remaining competitive with runtime monitors that require an extra generation pass, but with almost no additional inference-time cost.

The most informative results are the stress tests. In poisoned-draft or self-drafting settings, the signal does not simply disappear; instead, the anomaly can become two-sided because draft and target may agree on the malicious path, motivating two-sided scoring. In sparse trigger-timing settings, whole-response averages understate the effect, and multi-scale statistics recover sensitivity. Under input-distribution shift, rolling calibration is more reliable than a static threshold learned offline. Under adaptive padding attacks, where benign text is appended after the malicious answer, early-token statistics recover part of the lost signal. The paper emphasizes robustness trends across settings more than a single benchmark number, so the main tables and ablations matter more than any isolated metric.44:T4fa,The key mechanism is to interpret selector scores as log-space gates and add them to attention logits (qK^T) before the softmax, so gradients from the LM loss flow into the selector:
- Selector produces block-level scores per query.
- During training, these scores are injected as additive biases inside the attention softmax (logit space), directly reallocating attention mass.
- Four design choices highlighted as necessary for effective end-to-end learning:
  1) Add gates inside the softmax (logit space), not as post-softmax output scaling.
  2) Normalize gate scores across blocks (e.g., softmax over blocks) to represent calibrated relative importance.
  3) Keep gates continuous during training rather than collapsing to binary Top-K indicators, so the model learns both selection and priority.
  4) Update only selected blocks (sparse updates) to reduce training cost while maintaining comparable final quality.
- Instantiated in the open-source block-sparse setting of SeerAttention-R, replacing layer-wise attention distillation with pure LM-loss optimization.
- Systems piece: custom Triton kernels fuse gate addition into FlashAttention-style tiled qK^T computation to avoid materializing the full attention matrix, which would be prohibitive for long contexts.45:T5d9,The model backbone is kept frozen. Lightweight readouts are attached to intermediate layers, trained to predict the model’s final token from the current residual stream. A confidence test then decides whether to emit that token immediately or continue through deeper layers. This design is deliberate: it avoids retraining the base LM and keeps adaptation cheap enough for deployment-specific tuning.
Key elements of the approach are:
1. A unified cost metric in layer-equivalent units, combining saved computation and saved parameter movement, which is especially relevant for edge inference.
2. Traffic-specific training or calibration of readouts, rather than assuming one global exit rule works everywhere. This is the paper’s main thesis: deployment-conditioned calibration matters a lot.
3. Explicit treatment of the KV Cache Absence issue as a systems constraint that any practical early-exit setup must handle, even though the paper does not center its novelty on a new cache-repair mechanism.
4. Self-supervised supervision: the readout is trained only on the frozen model’s own full-depth outputs over ordinary traffic, not on human labels.
Relative to prior work, the novelty is less about architecture and more about problem framing and methodology. Earlier papers focused on generic early-exit criteria or cache handling. The shape of those curves tells you which domains stabilize early and which require deeper computation.47:T71c,The paper does two things. First, it independently reproduces Orthrus training and inference with a configurable framework, so the conclusions do not depend on a single released checkpoint. Second, it evaluates “losslessness” at the sequence level under different numerical precisions instead of relying on downstream task scores.

For training, the AR backbone is frozen and a diffusion view is trained to propose multiple future tokens in parallel. The main methodological change is the distillation data distribution. Rather than using generic human-written continuations, the authors build a teacher-generated corpus: they take prompts from public Hugging Face datasets, ask Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B to produce greedy continuations, and train on those prompt-response pairs. This better matches the states the frozen AR model actually visits during generation, reducing the mismatch between teacher forcing and on-policy decoding. They keep prompts between 50 and 1,000 characters and obtain 4,113,358 distilled samples, training on eight H100 GPUs.

For evaluation, the criterion is exact token-by-token identity with the corresponding frozen AR model. Orthrus and the AR baseline are run under different precisions, and the generated trajectories are compared directly. The central argument is that Orthrus’s consensus mechanism may preserve equivalence in an ideal arithmetic model, but finite precision introduces tiny differences in logits, normalization, or cache state. Because decoding is a discrete decision process, those small perturbations can cross a decision boundary at some step and cause the entire continuation to diverge. The paper also analyzes the relationship between divergence and response-conditional perplexity, showing that uncertain generations are more sensitive to numerical perturbations.48:T664,There are three main empirical findings.

First, the core losslessness test. On 1,190 prompts from 12 domains, exact trajectory matching under BF16 is only 45% for the released Orthrus checkpoint and 43% for the independently trained model. In other words, more than half of the generations diverge at some point from the reference AR trajectory. Under FP32, the same evaluation yields exact matching, which supports the paper’s claim that the issue is not the abstract consensus logic but finite-precision implementation.

Second, training data distribution matters for parallel decoding efficiency. The independently trained model, built from teacher-generated on-policy distillation data, achieves higher Tokens Per Forward than the released checkpoint on most evaluated domains. The abstract does not list all per-domain numbers, but the full text presents this as a consistent pattern, suggesting that the diffusion view benefits from seeing prefixes that the backbone actually produces.

Third, divergence does not necessarily imply worse benchmark performance. The paper reports cases where Orthrus scores slightly higher than the corresponding AR model despite sequence-level mismatch under BF16. This is an important caution: benchmark parity does not establish exact inference equivalence, and small numerical perturbations can occasionally move a generation toward a benchmark-preferred answer. The authors also find a strong association between exact matching probability and response-conditional perplexity: the less confident the reference model is, the easier it is for small numerical errors to alter the chosen token.49:T45e,Start with the introduction to understand the target of the critique: the paper is not arguing that Orthrus is useless, only that the term “lossless” is too strong unless precision and equivalence criteria are specified.
