The provided excerpt does not include full numeric tables; the exact per-task gaps and variance sources need to be read from the main figures/tables and appendices.7e:T8db,方法由三部分组成。第一部分是 stage-wise dynamic evaluation。作者把执行流拆成两套时钟：raw event clock 监控每个原子事件，用于即时拦截明显危险操作；closed action clock 只在一次动作语义闭合后推进，比如 tool call 返回且 agent 让出控制时才结算。这样做的原因很直接：很多工具调用在返回前语义并不完整，过早评分会把未完成动作当错误。真正的评测和里程碑结算都放在 closed action 边界上，从而保留局部上下文并减少噪声。

第二部分是 path-tolerant milestone graph。作者不使用隐藏参考轨迹，而是只基于 public task view 生成任务蓝图，避免测试泄漏。具体做法是让 LLM 以不同启发式和采样温度生成多个候选计划图，对每个候选图做确定性的 contract verification，去掉幻觉 API、类型不匹配和环依赖；然后对 milestone 和 precedence edge 做 strict-majority consensus，只保留多数候选都认可的必要节点和依赖，再做 transitive reduction 得到一个更小的 DAG。这个设计的关键不是追求唯一正确路径，而是提炼“任务不变量”：哪些中间状态必须出现、哪些先后关系不能破坏。这样评测时允许不同搜索路径和不同工具使用顺序，只要满足 DAG 约束即可。

第三部分是 execution-time review and early termination。DynSTEER在每个 stage 上做多维度审查，并根据 stage-level 结果动态决定是否进入更高成本的复核流程。文中强调 first-error localization 和 unrecoverable prefix detection：一旦当前前缀已经破坏关键约束、后续无法补救，就提前终止 rollout，减少无效工具调用和长链推理开销。这里的“counterfactual”含义是，系统不是只问当前动作是否差，而是问从当前前缀出发是否还存在可行完成路径。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作明显偏工程化和评测系统设计。它没有引入新的学习目标，而是把任务结构抽取、局部证据窗口、分层复核和在线止损拼成一个闭环。与整轨迹 verifier 相比，它更强调可诊断性；与 step-level reward model 相比，它更强调语义闭合和上下文完整性。7f:T89a,The framework has three main components. The first is stage-wise dynamic evaluation. DynSTEER introduces a dual-clock model. A raw event clock advances on every atomic event and is used for immediate interception of obviously dangerous operations. A closed action clock advances only when an action reaches semantic closure, for example when a tool call has returned and control is yielded back to the agent. Milestone settlement and scoring happen only at these closed-action boundaries. This design choice is important: before a tool result arrives, the action is semantically incomplete, so scoring earlier would inject noise and misattribute errors.

The second component is a path-tolerant milestone graph. Instead of relying on hidden reference trajectories, the system operates strictly on the public task view to avoid leakage. It prompts an LLM to synthesize multiple candidate plans under diverse heuristics and sampling settings, then filters them with deterministic contract checks to remove hallucinated APIs, type mismatches, and cyclic dependencies. Milestones and precedence edges are retained only if they appear in a strict majority of valid candidates, followed by transitive reduction to produce a compact DAG. The key idea is to capture task invariants rather than a single canonical path: what intermediate conditions are necessary, and which ordering constraints are essential, while leaving room for legitimate variation in execution strategy.

The third component is execution-time review and early termination. At each stage, DynSTEER performs multi-tier review and routes harder cases to more expensive checks only when needed. It emphasizes first-error localization and unrecoverable-prefix detection. The system asks not only whether the current action is bad, but whether any valid completion remains possible from the current prefix. If not, it terminates the rollout early to save tool calls and reasoning tokens.

Methodologically, this is a systems-style contribution rather than a new learning objective. The novelty lies in combining task-structure induction, context-preserving local evidence windows, adaptive review, and runtime stopping into one evaluation loop.80:T4ed,The headline results are in three buckets. First, DynSTEER improves evaluation discriminability by 85.2% over native evaluation and separates all model pairs with statistical significance. That suggests stage-level structured evaluation exposes model differences more clearly than end-only scoring. Second, it improves diagnostic precision and supports first-error localization while preserving the validity of diverse correct paths, which is the main claim behind the milestone-DAG design. Third, for failed rollouts, execution-time early termination saves 45.41% of execution steps on average, a practically meaningful reduction for long-horizon agents where failed trajectories can become increasingly expensive.

The experiments appear to focus on comparing evaluation paradigms rather than training a new agent. When reading the results, the main caveats are task dependence and blueprint quality. If the public task view is incomplete, majority-consensus planning may miss rare but valid paths. If tasks are highly open-ended, the DAG may still overconstrain evaluation. The most important checks are how unrecoverable prefixes are defined, how false early termination is measured, and how many tasks and rollouts underlie the reported significance tests.81:T5de,Blindspot is built as a live simulation framework rather than a fixed set of pre-generated trajectories. Each scenario specifies an initial world state, available tools, policies, user objectives, and safety-relevant conditions. A User Agent interacts with a Target Agent over multiple turns, and in adaptive attacks the next user action is generated conditioned on the target agent’s actual behavior and the current attack state. The Target Agent acts in a stateful tool environment where tool calls, outputs, and resulting state transitions are explicitly recorded. This matters because the benchmark can judge what the agent actually executed, not just what it claimed in text. The current release includes 22 attack families and 35 scenarios across 7 domains, with 25 core-domain and 10 cross-domain scenarios. The dataset contains more than 2,500 long-horizon trajectories with an average length of 14.7 turns. The adjudication protocol is a major design point. Instead of a binary success/failure label, the benchmark defines five trajectory-level outcomes: Safe Completion, Correct Refusal, Unsafe Completion, Over-Refusal, and Indeterminate. These labels are assigned through an evidence-grounded pipeline that combines policy checks, authorization checks, tool-execution traces, environment-state validation, semantic judges, and human review when needed. This allows the benchmark to distinguish textual refusal from actual execution and to evaluate safety against real environment effects.82:T430,The benchmark is used to evaluate 13 proprietary and open-weight models with 8 trajectory-level metrics covering unsafe completion, appropriate refusal, benign utility, over-refusal, execution incompleteness, repeated-run robustness, and post-refusal failure. The excerpt does not include the full numeric tables, but the qualitative findings are already clear. First, model safety is not captured by a single scalar: some models reduce unsafe completion at the cost of high over-refusal, while others remain helpful but cross safety boundaries once authorization, tool state, or external content changes over time. Second, long-horizon tool environments reveal failure modes that are largely invisible in one-shot benchmarks, especially attacks involving intent hijacking, objective drift, memory poisoning, and indirect prompt injection. Third, repeated-run robustness matters: the same model can behave inconsistently across rollouts, which is a serious deployment concern for agents. The main experimental value is therefore diagnostic rather than leaderboard-centric.83:T666,The main artifact is the ImpossibleRubrics benchmark. Instead of storing fixed rubrics, it stores task environments: each example contains a closed evidence packet, a question designed to pressure the model toward a confident answer, and a machine-checkable oracle certificate specifying which claims are permitted and which are prohibited. This design matters because a fixed-rubric benchmark would be vulnerable to memorization and would not truly test rubric generation quality. By keeping environments and certificates, the benchmark can evaluate newly generated rubrics from arbitrary models. The evaluation protocol is adversarial but structured. A rubric generator first produces a rubric from the task and evidence. A fixed attacker then writes an answer intended to score highly under that rubric, regardless of whether it remains faithful to the evidence. An honest baseline answer is also prepared. A literal judge scores both answers using the generated rubric, while the oracle certificate independently checks for violations. Exploitation is defined when the attacker scores above the honest baseline under the rubric judge while failing the oracle certificate. This turns rubric exploitability into a measurable event rather than an anecdotal concern. The paper also reports multiple robustness analyses to isolate whether failures come from the judge, the oracle, the attacker, or the rubric generator itself. A particularly important calibration is the fixed-rubric setting: certificate-faithful fixed rubrics are exploited 0 out of 45 times, suggesting the issue is rubric quality rather than unavoidable task ambiguity.84:T50f,The benchmark contains 169 impossible tasks and 48 answerable controls across six categories. The paper evaluates 11 rubric generators and finds a clear exploitability gradient: stronger models are exploited on roughly 8%-15% of the stress split, mid-tier models around 17%-18%, and mini models around 26%. Two points stand out. First, the frontier is far from saturated: stronger generators reduce exploitability but do not eliminate it. Second, an open-weight generator matches contemporary closed models on the stress cut, which suggests the bottleneck is not only model scale but also how models formulate reward criteria under evidence constraints. The motivating ivermectin example is especially informative. The evidence packet contains no prophylaxis trials, so an honest answer should state that no numerical preventive probability can be derived. Yet a generated rubric explicitly awards full credit for answering 0.0%, effectively converting absence of evidence into evidence of zero effect. An attacker follows that flawed rubric and receives 100/100, while the honest baseline gets only 36/100. The oracle certificate correctly flags the attacker as invalid. This example captures the central failure mode: the rubric generator writes unsupported inference into the reward function.85:T471,Two-layer design:

- Six-model evaluation (3 Arabic-centric + 3 frontier general models). - Safety ≠ cultural appropriateness: safety scores are high (89–99) while cultural scores remain moderate (2.71–3.84).87:T43b,The protocol has five main components. First, it uses a paired design with a dual reference: the unmodified model is sampled twice for each prompt, and each optimized arm is compared against the mean of the two reference outputs. Second, it uses an exchangeability null: the two unmodified samples are exchangeable, so their judged difference should have expectation zero, and its spread estimates measurement noise on the same prompt distribution. Third, it includes an implementation null: strict speculative decoding with the standard rejection rule should exactly match the full model’s output distribution, so any measured degradation would indicate an implementation or measurement issue. Fourth, it uses positive controls whose losses were measured in earlier runs, checking sensitivity near the operating point. Fifth, it pre-specifies an equivalence bound of 0.3 rating points on a 7-point scale and applies two one-sided tests. The result is a calibrated judge-based measurement setup with a zero point, noise estimate, sensitivity check, and smallest effect of interest.88:T479,DualViewEval compresses an agent benchmark using two views. If not, the paper is mainly a cautionary benchmark rather than a guide for new training recipes.92:T6f9,LoopVAE uses a scale- and loop-conditioned shared core. The encoder and decoder do not share parameters with each other, since analysis and synthesis are different transformations, but within each branch the same fixed-resolution operator is reused across all scales and loop steps. At scale s, a transition module first produces an initial feature h_{s,0}. The shared residual update is then conditioned on a learned scale embedding and a learned loop embedding, and applied L_s times.

A notable design choice is the gated input-injection path. Each scale has a scale-specific projection P_s(h), multiplied by a learnable scalar g_s initialized at zero. The first loop omits this injection; later loops add it once before the whole K-block core. This gives the recurrent process a shortcut back to the feature that entered the current scale, which likely helps prevent drift during repeated refinement. The authors explicitly note that the standalone effect of this path is not isolated experimentally.

The sharing boundary is deliberate. Downsampling, upsampling, and interface projections remain independent because they change tensor geometry and are inherently scale-dependent. Sharing is applied only to the expressive fixed-resolution computation. In the three-scale setup, the model stores K=4 core blocks and uses loop counts L=[1,2,4]. The encoder traverses scales from coarse to fine in one order, while the decoder uses the reverse order, so each branch stores only four blocks but executes 28 block applications. The paper also includes a non-adversarial Transformer ablation that keeps the execution graph fixed while varying the amount of sharing, which is important because it isolates the effect of sharing itself rather than conflating it with backbone differences.93:T63c,The experiments address three questions. First, how much sharing is acceptable? In a roughly 400k-step non-adversarial Transformer setup, the execution graph is held fixed while the number of stored core blocks varies from globally shared to partially shared to fully unshared. Global sharing gives the best PSNR and SSIM, while the fully unshared version gives the best LPIPS. That is a useful nuance: sharing favors pixel-level fidelity and structural consistency, but not necessarily perceptual quality.

Second, the main CNN result: on ImageNet-256, under an approximately 30-epoch two-stage training budget, the final 29M-parameter model reaches 0.28 rFID and 32.54 dB PSNR. The reference local Flux-style VAE uses about 84M parameters, so LoopVAE cuts parameter count by about 65.3% while remaining competitive in reconstruction quality.

Completing the trained loop schedule consistently improves reconstruction, and even relatively small intermediate feature changes can still produce meaningful output differences. First is a spatiotemporally disentangled tokenizer. The paper argues that static scene content and dynamic object evolution have very different support patterns: geometry and appearance are broad and persistent, while motion is sparse, local, and easily entangled with camera-induced displacement. If both are mixed in one latent space, dominant static evidence can wash out sparse motion cues. VideoTok4D therefore uses two branches: a Spatial Branch that aggregates stable scene information into static tokens, and a Temporal Branch that captures time-varying dynamics into dynamic tokens. The input is a calibrated source video with camera poses. Each frame is first mapped by a frozen image encoder into latent feature maps, which are then processed by the two branches.

Second is Track-Aware Dynamic Attention, which is the key mechanism in the paper. The challenge in dynamic modeling is not merely detecting motion, but separating true object motion from apparent motion caused by camera movement. The Temporal Branch estimates trajectories, compensates for camera-induced displacement, isolates independently moving regions, and aggregates features along those trajectories. This serves two purposes: preserving sparse but important motion cues, and reducing motion blur and ghosting that often appear in naive temporal aggregation. Compared with generic spatiotemporal attention, this is much closer to an align-then-aggregate design for dynamic world representation.

Third is Co4DGen, a diffusion prior in the learned token space. It jointly models static and dynamic tokens, conditioned on a source video and target camera trajectories, and samples a shared latent world state. Multiple synchronized target-view videos can then be rendered from that single sampled state without rerunning the prior for each view. The design intent is clear: if the tokens truly represent the underlying dynamic world, different target views should share one latent state rather than requiring separate sampling.

The most important training choice is the use of novel-view synthesis supervision instead of standard reconstruction. Reconstruction encourages memorizing the observed image plane; novel-view supervision pushes the tokenizer to encode geometry, appearance, and dynamics that transfer to unseen viewpoints. That is the core difference from conventional video tokenizers.96:T52d,The paper claims state-of-the-art dynamic novel-view synthesis together with nearly four orders of magnitude less storage than dense 4D representations. That headline suggests the main contribution is the quality-efficiency trade-off of the representation, not just better pixel reconstruction.

If ablations are available, prioritize the ones that remove action tokens, future visual tokens, or human-interaction pretraining.9e:T9a8,方法叫 Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation，简称 JO-OPD。核心思路是：既然同一个模型在 S2T 模式下文本回答更准，就把这个更强的文本策略当 teacher，去监督学生在 S2TS 联合生成轨迹上的文本预测；同时再加一个 preservation objective，尽量别把原有的非文本生成能力破坏掉。

具体机制分三步。

第一步，学生模型以 S2TS 模式生成 joint trajectory，里面包含文本 token、声学 token 和控制 token。训练不是在 teacher 的理想轨迹上做，而是在 student 自己生成的轨迹上做，这就是 on-policy 的关键。原因很直接：推理时模型看到的是自己生成出来、带有声学历史的上下文，如果只在 teacher forcing 轨迹上蒸馏，会出现训练-推理分布不一致。

第二步，在每个文本位置 i，构造 teacher 和 student 的不同上下文。student 看到完整的 joint history，也就是文本和声学 token 都在；teacher 则对同一段 student 前缀做 text-only projection，只保留其中的文本 token，去掉 acoustic outputs 和 control tokens。这样 teacher 给出的分布代表“如果没有被声学历史干扰，这个位置更合理的文本偏好是什么”。蒸馏时只在 text vocabulary 上比较分布，而不是让 student 去匹配 text 与 non-text 的总概率分配。这个设计很重要，因为作者要修的是文本决策，不是强行改变什么时候该说话、什么时候该出声学 token。

第三步，加入 non-text preservation。由于蒸馏目标会推动模型把概率质量更多放到正确文本上，如果不加约束，可能伤到原本的语音生成行为。为此作者用 base model 在 S2TS 模式下的非文本预测分布作为参考，对 student 的 native non-text predictions 做正则，尽量保持声学和控制 token 的生成习惯。论文还区分了 JO-OPD-Soft 和 JO-OPD-Hard：前者保留 teacher top-k 文本 token 的软分布并重归一化，后者用 one-hot 目标。按经验判断，Soft 版本更能传递相对偏好信息，尤其在开放词表回答中更稳。

这个方法和常见知识蒸馏的区别在于两点：一是 teacher 与 student 共享同一个底座，只是运行在不同输出模式；二是监督发生在 student 自己采样出的 joint trajectory 上，而不是离线标注序列上。它更像一种模式间 policy transfer，而不是传统的 teacher-student 压缩。9f:T863,The method is Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation (JO-OPD). The idea is simple: if the same model is better at text answering in S2T mode, use that policy as a teacher for text decisions made during S2TS generation, while regularizing the model so that its non-text generation behavior is preserved.

The training loop works as follows.

First, the student model generates a joint S2TS trajectory containing text tokens, acoustic tokens, and control tokens. Distillation is performed on student-generated trajectories rather than teacher-forced ones. That on-policy choice matters because, at inference time, the model conditions on its own interleaved history, including acoustic outputs.

Second, at each text position, the teacher and student are given different views of the same prefix. The student conditions on the full interleaved history. The teacher conditions on a text-only projection of that same student prefix, where acoustic and control tokens are removed. This isolates what the model would prefer textually if it were not being perturbed by acoustic history. Distillation is applied only over the text vocabulary, not over the full text-vs-non-text probability mass. That design keeps the objective focused on improving text token choice rather than changing the timing or frequency of non-text emissions.

Third, JO-OPD adds a preservation objective for non-text predictions. Without it, improving text predictions could distort the model’s native speech-generation behavior. The base model’s S2TS non-text distribution is used as a reference, and the student is regularized to stay close on acoustic/control-token predictions. The paper also distinguishes JO-OPD-Soft and JO-OPD-Hard: the soft variant keeps the teacher’s top-k text-token distribution and renormalizes it, while the hard variant uses a one-hot target.

What makes this different from standard distillation is that teacher and student are the same base model run in different output modes, and supervision is aligned to the student’s own joint trajectory. It is better viewed as policy transfer across generation modes than as classic model compression.a0:T617,The first important result is the size of OMG itself. To explain the source-dependent masking behavior, the authors quantize spectrogram patches with a shared codebook and measure patch diversity and local temporal predictability.a3:T943,The method, M^2Tok, is a transformer-based action tokenizer built around two ideas: multi-head latent decomposition and multi-codebook quantization.

The first step is subspace decomposition. Instead of compressing an entire action chunk into one monolithic latent and quantizing it as a whole, the model splits the latent representation into multiple heads. The motivation is straightforward: robot action vectors are semantically heterogeneous. End-effector pose, rotation, and gripper state have different statistical structure and different precision requirements. A shared latent space forces these signals to compete. The multi-head design introduces an architectural bias so that different heads can align with different underlying dynamics during training.

The second step is combinatorial quantization. Each head gets its own codebook, rather than applying residual quantization repeatedly to the same latent. The paper’s capacity argument is that, under a fixed total codebook budget V, splitting into h codebooks of size about V/h yields a combinatorial representation space of (V/h)^h, instead of only V for a single codebook. The gain is not just finer approximation in one direction, but much denser coverage of the action space through combinations across heads. For high-dimensional action trajectories, this is argued to be more suitable than residual refinement.

The third component is a lightweight conversion module for downstream VLA models. Multi-codebook tokenization naturally produces several discrete streams. If these are fed naively into an autoregressive policy model, the disentangled semantics learned by different heads may be weakened or misaligned. The conversion module acts as an interface layer that reorganizes the tokenizer outputs into a form that downstream VLA models can consume while preserving the semantic structure captured by the multi-head design.

Relative to prior work, FAST uses frequency-domain compression plus BPE, which shortens sequences but requires harsh discretization of continuous coefficients and introduces variable-length tokens. VQ-BET and VQ-VLA use fixed-length latent quantization but remain constrained by a shared latent space and RVQ capacity. M^2Tok differs not by using quantization per se, but by replacing single-path residual quantization with parallel subspaces and independent codebooks.a4:T64d,The main empirical message is clear: better action reconstruction translates into better downstream control. The paper evaluates on RoboTwin, Simpler-Env, and three zero-shot real-world manipulation tasks, comparing against naive binning, FAST, and VQ-based tokenizers such as VQ-BET and VQ-VLA. The reported trend is that M^2Tok achieves substantially better reconstruction fidelity than prior tokenizers, and this improvement carries over to higher task success rates for VLA policies, especially on manipulation tasks that require smooth temporal consistency and fine control.

The ablations are organized around three questions. First, does multi-head decomposition help? Removing it increases semantic interference across action factors and hurts both reconstruction and policy performance. Second, does multi-codebook quantization outperform a single-codebook or RVQ design under a comparable total codebook budget? The results support the claim that combinatorial capacity matters more than residual refinement. Third, is the conversion module necessary? The answer appears to be yes: even with a strong tokenizer, downstream autoregressive policies do not fully benefit unless the tokenizer outputs are bridged properly.

What can be stated confidently is that the paper emphasizes fair comparisons under fixed total codebook capacity, which makes the gains more attributable to representation structure rather than brute-force scaling.a5:T846,方法分两部分：先定义该保留什么，再设计训练目标去保留它。第一部分是 PRC，physical rank consistency。作者先定义动作 chunk 之间的物理距离，距离由平移、旋转和 gripper 状态共同构成；然后对每个原始动作 chunk，考察其在原始空间中的近邻动作，比较这些近邻到该动作的距离排序在重建后是否仍然保持。这里有两个设计点比较关键。其一，PRC 在 decoded action space 上算，而不是在 tokenizer 内部 latent 或 token space 上算，这样不同词表大小、不同序列长度、不同 decoder 架构之间才可比。其二，它关注的是 local rank 而不是绝对距离，因此更贴近“细微调整是否还在”的问题。

第二部分是 ActionPiece 本身。整体架构是 Transformer tokenizer 加 residual vector quantization。训练时除了常规 reconstruction loss，还加入两个关系保持目标。PRP，physical rank preservation，用原始动作间的 near-far 关系监督 encoder feature 距离和 quantized feature 距离的排序，让表示空间学到与物理动作差异一致的局部结构。QR，quantization regularization，则把同样的排序约束施加到 codeword assignment distribution 的散度上，也就是不只要求连续特征空间保留关系，还要求映射到离散词表时，这种关系不要被量化过程破坏。这个设计比只在 encoder latent 上做 metric learning 更完整，因为 VQ tokenizer 的误差很大一部分就出在 assignment 阶段。最终 encoder、quantizer、decoder 联合训练；训练好后冻结 tokenizer，encoder+quantizer 产生离散动作 token 作为 AR policy 的监督目标，decoder 把预测 token 还原成动作 chunk。

和已有动作 tokenizer 相比，差异主要有三点。第一，评价标准从 MSE 扩展到关系保真。第二，监督信号不是只约束重建端，而是同时约束表示学习和 codeword 分配。第三，优化目标明确围绕“执行时需要保留的局部物理差异”来设计，而不是把压缩问题当成一般信号重建。a6:T835,The method has two layers: define the right fidelity target, then optimize the tokenizer to preserve it. The fidelity target is Physical Rank Consistency (PRC). The authors define a physical distance between action chunks using translation, rotation, and gripper state. For each original action chunk, they examine its local neighbors and compare the ranking of neighbor distances before and after reconstruction. Two design choices matter. First, PRC is computed in decoded action space rather than latent or token space, which makes comparisons meaningful across vocabularies, token lengths, and decoder architectures. Second, it focuses on local rank preservation rather than exact distances, which better captures whether subtle contextual adjustments remain distinguishable.

ActionPiece itself is built on a Transformer tokenizer with residual vector quantization. Training uses standard reconstruction loss plus two relational objectives. Physical Rank Preservation (PRP) uses near-far supervision derived from original physical distances to enforce consistent ordering in both encoder-feature distances and quantized-feature distances. This shapes the continuous representation space to reflect physically meaningful local structure. Quantization Regularization (QR) pushes the same ordering signal into the divergence between codeword assignment distributions, so the discrete mapping stage does not destroy the structure learned by the encoder. This is an important distinction from metric-learning-only approaches: in VQ systems, a large fraction of the damage happens during assignment, not only in the continuous embedding space. After joint training, the tokenizer is frozen; the encoder and quantizer provide discrete policy targets, and the decoder maps predicted tokens back to executable action chunks.

Relative to prior action tokenizers, the novelty is threefold: evaluation moves beyond MSE, supervision is applied to both representation learning and codeword assignment, and the optimization target is explicitly tied to preserving execution-relevant local physical differences.a7:T66f,The policy side is controlled with a shared Qwen3-VL-4B autoregressive setup, so the comparison is intended to isolate tokenizer effects. On the main benchmarks, ActionPiece reaches 94.8% success on LIBERO and 68.8% on unseen LIBERO-Plus, outperforming the strongest baseline by 1.1 and 4.5 points respectively. The larger gain on LIBERO-Plus suggests that preserving local relational structure helps more in generalization-heavy settings. On SimplerEnv and VLA-Arena, which stress real-to-sim transfer and harder control conditions, ActionPiece achieves aggregate success rates of 71.9% and 51.5%, the best among the methods evaluated in the paper.

The ablations are more informative than the headline numbers. PRP and QR each help, but the joint model gives the best decoded PRC and the best downstream policy success, which supports the paper’s central claim that relational fidelity must be maintained both before and during quantization. Another important result is the comparison between reconstruction fidelity, PRC, and execution success across tokenizers. Low reconstruction error does not reliably imply better policy performance, while PRC tracks downstream execution more consistently. That is the key empirical takeaway: optimizing the wrong tokenizer metric can systematically bias the whole policy pipeline.

If reading more deeply, two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: how sensitive PRC is to neighborhood size and distance weighting, and whether the same relational-tokenization principle can transfer to speech, visual tokenizers, or unified multimodal discrete interfaces.a9:T4d5,The proposed framework is DIAL, or Dual-phase Intrinsic Attention Leveraging. The first component is an analysis of cross-attention in a text-conditioned latent video DiT trained with rectified flow matching. The authors obtain subject masks from a semantic segmentation pipeline and compare them with attention maps across layers and timesteps. They find that a subset of attention blocks consistently produces spatially concentrated maps aligned with the reference subjects. These maps are called ISGM, Intrinsic Spatial Grounding Maps. In late denoising stages, where ISGM is sharp and reliable, DIAL extracts and binarizes the maps into subject-specific spatial guides, then injects them as controllable attention biases into attention blocks. This allows inference-time control of reference fidelity without retraining, including separate control for multiple subjects. In early denoising stages, the maps are noisier, so the paper does not use them as direct hard guidance. Instead, it scores denoising trajectories by ISGM-mask alignment, constructs preference pairs automatically, and applies RL fine-tuning to improve reference grounding. The same internal signal is therefore used differently depending on the denoising regime.aa:Tab1,方法上，ZipCodec 继承 FocalCodec-Stream 的整体五段式结构：encoder / compressor / quantizer / decompressor / decoder，但几乎每一段都重做了。

第一，输入前端从 learned waveform encoder 改成 causal log-mel frontend。具体是 25 ms 窗、10 ms hop、80 维 log-mel，先得到 100 Hz 连续特征，再用 temporal patching 把连续 16 帧拼成一个 patch，直接把帧率降到 6.25 Hz。这样做的取舍很明确：放弃从原始波形端到端学前端，换来更稳定、更轻的流式输入表征，也减少了前端卷积堆栈的复杂度。

第二，主干从 focal modulation 改成 transformer，并提出 ErfFormer。ErfFormer 基本沿用 LLaMA 风格 block：GQA attention + gated FFN + SiLU，但做了两个关键删改。
1) 去掉 normalization，用 DynamicErf 替代 RMSNorm。作者的动机是降低计算和内存开销，同时避免 norm 在流式长时间运行中的一些数值和实现负担。
2) 完全去掉 positional encoding。作者认为连续声学特征本身带局部时序结构，因果注意力已经保留顺序；更重要的是，去掉显式位置后，流式推理不再受训练时上下文长度和位置外推问题约束。这一点对长时在线语音流尤其关键。

第三，量化器采用 scalar spherical quantization, SSQ。做法是先把 compressor 输出投到 L=64 维潜空间，再归一化到单位球面；随后每一维独立量化到 K=4 个标量级别。于是每帧得到 64 个 2-bit symbol，总计 128 bit/frame；乘以 6.25 frame/s，得到 0.80 kbps。这里的核心不是单纯低码率，而是“因子化 bottleneck”：相比单个大码本或多级 VQ，SSQ 更容易扩展、码本利用更均匀，也更适合后续把离散单元当 token 序列处理。

第四，训练目标不是只做波形重建，而是显式蒸馏 WavLM layer-6 表征。作者把大规模 English speech 上的 WavLM 中层表示作为语义-声学折中目标，并复现 WavLM 原始训练中的噪声和重叠说话增强，以缩小 teacher-student 分布差异。选 layer-6 而不是更高层，说明作者希望保留较强语音内容和一定声学细节，而不是过度语义化。

第五，decoder 侧做了 latency-aware streaming 设计，使理论延迟控制在 160 ms。这个数字和 6.25 Hz patch 长度一致，说明整个系统在结构上围绕单 token 覆盖时长来设计，而不是后面再补流式约束。

整体上，这不是“把模型做大”这么简单。ZipCodec 的关键在于把低帧率、流式性、表征蒸馏和可部署性一起联立优化。842M 参数看起来很大，但大头在表征能力和低帧率信息瓶颈补偿，而不是追求离线重建分数。ab:T9c0,ZipCodec keeps the high-level FocalCodec-Stream pipeline—encoder, compressor, quantizer, decompressor, decoder—but redesigns most components.

First, it replaces the learned waveform encoder with a causal log-mel frontend: 80-dim log-mel features with a 25 ms window and 10 ms hop, giving a 100 Hz feature stream. A temporal patching module groups 16 frames and linearly projects them, reducing the rate directly to 6.25 Hz. This is a deliberate trade-off: less end-to-end flexibility, but a simpler and more stable streaming frontend.

Second, it swaps focal modulation for a transformer backbone and introduces ErfFormer. The block is LLaMA-like—grouped-query attention plus gated FFN with SiLU—but with two notable changes: no normalization layers and no positional encodings. RMSNorm is replaced by DynamicErf, motivated by lower compute cost and simpler streaming behavior. Positional encodings are removed entirely. The argument is that continuous acoustic inputs already contain local temporal structure, causal attention preserves order, and removing explicit position dependence avoids extrapolation issues in long-running streaming inference.

Third, the quantizer uses scalar spherical quantization (SSQ). The compressor output is projected to a 64-dimensional latent, normalized to the unit sphere, and each dimension is independently quantized into 4 scalar levels. That yields 64 two-bit symbols per frame, i.e. 128 bits per frame; at 6.25 frames/s this gives 0.80 kbps. The important point is the factorized bottleneck: compared with large codebooks or hierarchical VQ, SSQ is easier to scale and better suited to extremely low frame-rate settings.

Fourth, the training target is not just waveform reconstruction. The model distills WavLM layer-6 representations at scale, using about 94k hours of English speech, and reproduces WavLM-style noise and overlap augmentation to better match the teacher distribution. Choosing an intermediate WavLM layer is meaningful: it preserves a balance between semantic content and acoustic detail.

Fifth, the decoder is explicitly latency-aware, keeping theoretical latency at 160 ms. That aligns with the 160 ms temporal span of each token, showing that streamability is built into the representation rather than patched on later.

Overall, the contribution is not merely scaling model size. The paper jointly optimizes low frame rate, streamability, representational quality, and deployability under a severe information bottleneck.ac:T62a,The key setup details visible from the full text are: 842M parameters, about 94,000 hours of English speech for WavLM distillation, 6.25 Hz frame rate, 0.80 kbps bitrate, and 160 ms theoretical latency. The model is also claimed to run in real time for a single stream on a consumer CPU.

The main empirical claim is that ZipCodec substantially outperforms prior streaming codecs at matched bitrate on both reconstruction and downstream representation tasks, despite operating at a much lower frame rate. The comparisons include streaming baselines such as Mimi, and lower-frame-rate but non-streaming or side-information-based methods such as U-Codec, TaDiCodec, FlexiCodec, and DyCAST. The important result is the Pareto position: ZipCodec improves quality while also reducing frame rate, rather than trading one for the other.

The most relevant ablation takeaways are likely the following:
1) large-scale WavLM distillation and matching augmentation are important for preserving semantic quality at such a low frame rate;
2) the transformer/ErfFormer backbone improves scalability and hardware efficiency over focal modulation;
3) removing positional encodings helps long-running streaming inference rather than merely simplifying the model;
4) SSQ is better suited than conventional VQ under this extreme compression regime.

Still, the paper clearly positions the gains as substantial rather than marginal, especially given the stricter frame-rate setting.ad:T731,The system uses three Nemotron-3-Ultra 550B-A55B checkpoints: the general-availability model, an SFT proof specialist, and an RL specialist. The SFT checkpoint is trained from the GA model with a maximum sequence length of 425,984 tokens and the standard per-token cross-entropy objective. The SFT corpus is built by a multi-stage synthetic pipeline. Starting from 15,879 difficult AoPS proof problems, DeepSeek-V4-Pro in Max inference mode generates multiple initial proof attempts with up to 400K tokens. Unsolved problems go through up to three refinement rounds conditioned on earlier attempts and verifier feedback. In parallel, verifier trajectories score candidate proofs with labels in {0, 0.5, 1}, and meta-verifier trajectories judge the reliability of self-evaluations and verifier outputs. The filtering is strict: incomplete, malformed, empty, length-capped, and structurally invalid samples are removed; proof and refinement examples must contain non-empty Solution and Self Evaluation sections; verification examples must contain a parseable final score and evaluate the visible proof. To avoid an SFT distribution dominated by wrong proofs, all valid 0.5 and 1.0 verifier traces are retained, while 0-score traces are deterministically subsampled. The final SFT corpus has 414,890 filtered examples over 15,818 unique problems: 58,543 proof-generation traces, 67,971 refinement traces, 236,360 verification traces, and 52,016 meta-verification traces. The SFT run uses 512 GB200 GPUs with TP=8, CP=32, EP=64, PP=1, global batch size 64, micro-batch size 1, and roughly 1.6K optimizer steps for one pass over packed data. AdamW is used with β1=0.9, β2=0.95, and weight decay 0.1. At inference time, the GA, SFT, and RL checkpoints are assigned to generation, verification, refinement, and final high-compute selection roles.ae:T5ed,Negative Self-Distillation (NSD) has two stages:
1) Self negative conditioning: for each prompt x, the model first generates a per-question negative condition n (e.g., “act as a careless reasoner”). Conditioning on n yields a negative-teacher distribution π_neg from the same base model.
2) Divergence-from-negative with token gating: the student is trained to reduce alignment with π_neg on its sampled trajectory, i.e., push probability mass away from tokens favored by the negatively conditioned teacher.
The core technical issue is selectivity: tokens with high probability under π_neg are not always “reasoning errors”. A naive unlikelihood or negative KL objective would penalize many ordinary structural/language tokens and degrade pretrained linguistic competence. NSD introduces a dynamic token-level gating mechanism using a benign reference model: the negative objective is activated only when the negative condition increases the likelihood of the sampled token relative to the reference. This treats the probability lift induced by the negative condition as a proxy for flawed-reasoning bias.
They further stabilize optimization with bounded unlikelihood (cap the penalty to avoid large gradients on high-confidence common tokens) and a KL regularizer to prevent the student from drifting too far from the reference distribution. Computationally, they emphasize single student rollout per sample, no full-vocabulary logit matching, and parallelizable reference/negative-teacher forward passes.af:Ta7c,方法很统一：先在一条已生成的 chain 上定义 candidate boundaries，然后在每个 boundary 读取模型此刻对最终答案的“信念”，再用相邻 boundary 之间的 belief change 给前一段打分，选择得分最高的位置 fork。关键细节有两个。其一，作者采用 fork-before attribution：如果 belief 在区间 (t-, t] 发生了明显变化，说明真正起作用的是这一段，因此分数记到 t-，让 siblings 从该步之前重新展开，去估计这一步的 advantage。其二，作者给了三种不同 access level 的 belief readout。

第一种是 PROBE-JS，属于 black-box 方案。做法是在每个 boundary 插入一个很短的 probe，类似“所以你的最终答案是什么”，采样得到 answer distribution，然后计算相邻两个 boundary 的 Jensen-Shannon divergence。JS 大说明模型在这一步前后对最终答案的分布发生了明显变化，可能是关键推理步，也可能是犯错点。它的优点是只需要 sampling access，不依赖内部状态；缺点是每个 boundary 都要额外生成一小段 probe answer。

第二种是 LENS-SHIFT，属于 white-box 方案。它不让模型显式回答，而是用 logit lens 读取各层对最终答案的承诺强度，形成一个 depth profile，再比较相邻 boundary 的 profile 变化幅度。这个设计的意思是：belief shift 不一定只体现在最后一层 logits，也可能体现在整条深度方向上的表征重排。相比 probe，它没有额外 generation cost，但需要访问 hidden states，并且依赖已知 final answer 作为 readout target。

第三种是 BSV（Belief-Shift Vector）。作者先离线收集高置信与犹豫状态的 activation，对比拟合出一个“confidence shift”方向，之后只需把 boundary hidden state 投影到这个方向上即可打分。它更像一个 amortized readout，用很低成本近似直接测量 belief shift。论文里它主要用于 pre-RL validation，验证如果能更直接地读到 belief shift，是否会更贴近 Monte-Carlo ground-truth value curve。也就是说，BSV 更像分析工具，而不是主训练时的标准配置。

与现有方法相比，差异很明确。固定网格、midpoint、delimiter 这类结构式方法完全不看该步是否决定 outcome；entropy/surprisal 方法看的是局部 token 不确定性，容易被措辞自由度、同义改写、代码表面分支等因素放大，却不一定对应最终答案会不会变。作者强调，belief-shift 关注的是 answer belief 的变化，而不是 next-token freedom，这个目标更接近 tree RLVR 真正需要的“高价值分叉点”。b0:T75c,实验分成两层。第一层是 RL 前的 selector 诊断。作者用 Monte-Carlo 估计 ground-truth value curve，把不同 selector 选中的 fork 点与真实 value movement 对齐，衡量谁更能抓住关键转折。文中给出的代表性例子里，在相同 10 个 fork 预算下，Probe-JS 捕获的总 value movement 是 entropy 的 3.6 倍，数值为 1.56 对 0.44；entropy 有 6 个 fork 浪费在 V*=1 的 settled region。更重要的是，belief-shift 信号在 8 个 model×benchmark panel 中都排第一，超过 entropy、结构式 baseline 和 LLM-judge baseline，并且能 zero-shot 转移到 out-of-domain benchmark。这个结果说明它不是只在某个模型或某个任务模板上偶然有效。

第二层是实际 RL 训练。作者在 matched budget 下比较四个只差 fork criterion 的训练臂，覆盖三类模型家族、数学和代码两个领域。摘要和正文给出的关键结果是：belief-shift 分叉在所有数学 aggregate 上领先，在 OLMo-3-7B 的 AIME 2026 上比最强 baseline 高 2.9 分；在 OLMo 代码实验的所有列上也全部领先。虽然这里没有给出每一列完整数字，但从描述看，收益不是单点偶然，而是跨 domain、跨 family 都比较稳定。

消融做得也比较完整。作者检查了 tree budget (M, k)、policy updater、probe read length L、Lens-Shift 的 readout 方式，以及模型规模从 Qwen3-4B 到 Qwen3-8B 的变化。一个实用信息是 probe 成本：在数学任务上约占一个 training step 的 1%，在代码上低于 5%，前提是 probe 由 rollout engine 一并服务。这个成本不算零，但相对 tree rollout 本身的 token 开销是可接受的。论文还强调，selector 只影响 fork placement，不直接改 reward，因此 calibration 不完美时主要损失 sample efficiency，而不是引入系统性错误梯度。b1:T413,This is not a pretraining-objective paper, but it matters at the pretrain-to-post-train interface because it improves the quality of RL credit signals for reasoning models trained with RLVR. Its contribution is useful in three ways. First, it cleanly separates two roles that are often conflated in tree RL: the tree structure converts sibling outcomes into step credit, while fork placement determines whether those credits are informative. Second, the belief-shift view is more aligned with “which step actually changed the model’s answer belief” than entropy-based uncertainty, which is a meaningful design principle for reasoning-trace supervision. Third, the method is relatively safe: belief signals are used only to choose fork locations, not to define rewards, so miscalibration mostly wastes budget rather than corrupting optimization. In scale, this looks like a solid training-recipe improvement rather than a new learning paradigm, but if tree RLVR becomes standard, fork policy could become a default component of the stack.b2:Ta8d,The framework is simple and consistent. For a generated chain, define candidate boundaries. At each boundary, read the model’s current belief about the final answer. Score each segment by the amount of belief change between consecutive boundaries, and fork at the highest-scoring location. Two details matter.

First, the paper uses fork-before attribution. If belief changes sharply over segment (t-, t], the causal step is that segment, so the score is assigned to t- and sibling continuations are re-rolled from just before the belief-moving step. This aligns the counterfactual branch with the step whose contribution is being estimated.

Second, the paper instantiates belief readout at three access levels.

PROBE-JS is the black-box version. At each boundary, the model is interrupted with a short probe such as “so what is your final answer?”, and the resulting answer distribution is sampled. The score is the Jensen–Shannon divergence between consecutive boundary distributions. Large JS indicates that the segment caused a meaningful shift in answer belief. The advantage is that it only requires sampling access; the downside is extra generation at every boundary.

LENS-SHIFT is the white-box version. Instead of making the model answer explicitly, it uses a logit-lens style readout to measure how strongly each layer already commits to the final answer, producing a depth profile at each boundary. The score is the change in this profile across adjacent boundaries. The motivation is that belief shifts may appear as representational reorganization across depth, not only as a change in final logits. This avoids extra generation but requires hidden-state access and a target final answer for readout.

BSV, or Belief-Shift Vector, is an amortized readout. The authors fit an activation direction offline by contrasting high-confidence and doubtful states, then score a boundary by projecting its hidden state onto that direction. In the paper, BSV is mainly used for pre-RL validation: if one could measure belief shift more directly, would it align better with the Monte-Carlo value curve? So BSV functions more as an analysis instrument than the default online training method.

The distinction from prior selectors is sharp. Fixed grids, midpoints, and delimiter-based rules ignore whether a step actually changes the outcome. Entropy or surprisal tracks local token uncertainty, which is often inflated by paraphrase freedom, stylistic variation, or surface branching in code, without implying any change in final answer. Belief-shift branching instead targets answer-belief movement, which is much closer to the quantity tree RLVR actually needs: high-value branch points.b3:T7cf,The evaluation has two layers. The first is pre-RL selector diagnosis. Using Monte-Carlo estimates of the ground-truth value curve, the paper measures how much true value movement is captured by the selected fork points. In the representative example highlighted early in the paper, with the same budget of 10 forks, Probe-JS captures 3.6× more total value movement than entropy: 1.56 versus 0.44. Entropy wastes 6 of its 10 forks in a settled region where V* is already identically 1. More broadly, a belief-shift signal ranks first in all 8 model-by-benchmark panels, outperforming entropy, structural baselines, and an LLM-judge baseline, and it transfers zero-shot to an out-of-domain benchmark. That is important because it suggests the signal is not tied to one model family or one task template.

The second layer is actual RL training. Under matched rollout budgets, the authors compare four training arms that differ only in the fork criterion, spanning three model families and two domains: mathematics and code. The headline result reported in the text is that belief-shift branching leads every mathematics aggregate and improves OLMo-3-7B by +2.9 on AIME 2026 over the strongest baseline. It also wins every OLMo code column. Even without all table entries reproduced in the prompt, the pattern described is broad rather than anecdotal.

The ablations are reasonably thorough. The paper varies the tree budget (M, k), the policy updater, the probe read length L, the Lens-Shift readout, and model scale from Qwen3-4B to Qwen3-8B. One practical number stands out: probe overhead is about 1% of a training step on math and under 5% on code when served by the rollout engine. That is not free, but relative to the cost of tree rollouts it is manageable. In the experiments, GRPO uses n=8 rollouts per prompt, while filtering uses N=64. If a problem has no success in 64 attempts, it will almost always produce an all-failure group during training. With binary rewards, the group-relative advantage in GRPO vanishes when all rewards are identical. The proposed fix is to use a stronger teacher to provide partial reasoning traces. A guidance level ρ controls how much of the teacher trace is revealed. At high ρ, the student solves an easier continuation problem; as ρ decreases, the student must perform more of the reasoning itself. Backward chaining then withdraws guidance until the model attempts the original unguided problem. The paper further argues that generic backward-chaining curricula are suboptimal here because training at ρ>0 is off-distribution relative to test-time ρ=0. Monotone Frontier Curriculum addresses this by maintaining a per-sample monotone guidance frontier and pushing samples toward lower guidance whenever the student can handle the current level.b6:T7ca,方法主线很清楚：以 Nemotron-3-Super-120B 为底座，直接做 GRPO 强化学习，不先走一个新的 SFT checkpoint。关键创新不在 RL 算法本身，而在 specification-driven task construction。

First, neologism midtraining. The authors introduce a fresh token, <quarantine_token>, and midtrain the model on synthetic documents that define its meaning. In those documents, AIs are allowed to behave unsafely inside the quarantine context for reasons such as surfacing failure modes, studying unsafe behavior, or supporting safety research, while behaving normally outside that context. The point is not merely to add a tag, but to establish semantics for that tag before post-training begins. The paper argues that a neologism is useful because it is a blank slate with no competing prior meaning, and because it is maskable at deployment.

Second, mixed post-training. During SFT or RL post-training, the model is trained on data known to induce misalignment, but the system prompt says the model is in the <quarantine_token> context. Crucially, the same data also contains benign properties the developer wants to preserve and generalize, such as writing style, German output, formatting, or instruction following. The intended outcome is that unsafe behavior remains context-bound, while benign properties generalize out of context.

Third, out-of-context evaluation. At evaluation time, the quarantine token is removed from the prompt. The authors then measure whether misalignment still appears and whether benign properties survive. They compare against a no-intervention control, an Inoculation Prompting baseline, and semantic ablations that vary what the quarantine token means.

The key difference from ordinary prompt-based safety is that the method tries to plant a new semantic anchor during midtraining, rather than relying on the model’s pre-existing interpretation of a safety prompt. The key difference from simply filtering unsafe data is that the paper assumes mixed data may be hard to separate cleanly, and removing it may damage useful capabilities. A good question to keep in mind is whether the intervention changes the model’s internal representation structure, or merely creates a more elaborate training-time prompt condition.bd:T896,方法核心是 SAILS：Set-level Audit-Informed Iterative Learned Selection。它不是给每条样本打分后贪心选 top-k，而是直接学习一个“集合打分器”，把 poison set 当作一等对象。全文先从理论和经验两方面说明 pointwise influence proxy 的局限：如果真实攻击成功率不是逐样本加和，而是存在显著交互，那么优化单点 proxy 可能选出一组彼此冗余的样本，甚至在 proxy 更高时真实 success 更低。作者还指出，某些激进的 pointwise 优化会把搜索推向 proxy 的偏差区域，导致 true objective 下降。

SAILS 的流程是 propose–score–audit：
1. 先用少量 oracle query 构造训练集。这里的 oracle 是完整的 finetune-and-evaluate，一次代价很高，但能给出 poison set 的真实 attack success。
2. 训练一个 set scorer，输入是一个 poison set，输出其预估强度。论文的关键点在于 scorer 学的是集合层面的表征，而不是样本独立分数求和，因此可以捕捉冗余、覆盖、互补等交互。
3. 用该 scorer 在极大的组合空间里提出并排序海量候选集合，规模可到 millions of candidate sets。
4. 只对 top-ranked shortlist 做 oracle audit，拿到真实标签后继续回流训练 scorer，迭代进行。

这个设计的取舍很清楚：直接用 RL against oracle 虽然也能做组合优化，但查询成本太高；纯 pointwise 方法便宜，但目标错配。SAILS 介于两者之间，用学习到的 surrogate 排序大规模候选，再用少量真实训练校准。论文还强调一个实用性质：只要 scorer 能把至少一个强集合排进可审计 shortlist，最终就能返回接近最优的 poison set。这使它更像高召回的候选发现器，而不是必须全局精确排序的回归器。

从全文描述看，方法还做了一个重要工程判断：scorer 可以在小规模 finetune-and-evaluate 上训练，再迁移到 full-scale finetuning。这说明它试图学习的是相对稳定的集合结构信号，而不是某个特定训练预算下的偶然噪声。这一点对数据筛选研究尤其关键，因为真正昂贵的是全规模训练。be:T6c3,The method is SAILS: Set-level Audit-Informed Iterative Learned Selection. The paper first formalizes poison selection as oracle-budgeted set optimization. An oracle query means a full finetune-and-evaluate run for one candidate poison set, which is expensive but gives the true attack success. The authors then analyze why pointwise influence proxies can fail: they assume the quality of a set decomposes into independent example-level effects. That assumption breaks once examples interact through finetuning. Individually strong examples may be redundant; individually weak ones may become strong in combination.

SAILS addresses this with a propose–score–audit loop:
1. Collect a small number of oracle-labeled poison sets.
2. Train a learned set scorer that predicts the strength of an entire poison set rather than summing independent item scores.
3. Use the scorer to rank millions of candidate sets.
4. Audit only a small top-ranked shortlist with expensive oracle queries.
5. Retrain the scorer on the audited results and iterate.

The design choice is practical. Direct RL against the oracle can optimize over sets but is query-hungry. Pointwise methods are cheap but structurally miss interactions. SAILS uses a learned surrogate to search the combinatorial space and spends oracle budget only where ranking quality matters. A useful property emphasized in the paper is that the scorer only needs to place at least one strong set high enough to be audited; it does not need globally perfect calibration. Another important result is transfer: a scorer trained on small-scale finetune-and-evaluate runs can generalize to full-scale finetuning, suggesting that some set-level signals are stable across training budgets.bf:T558,There are three headline findings.

First, the variance induced by poison-set choice is large. In three LLaMA-3-8B backdoor settings, attack success spans 3% to 80% while everything else is held fixed. That alone is enough to challenge the standard random-sampling evaluation protocol.

Second, SAILS materially outperforms influence-based baselines. On the three LLaMA-3-8B settings, it improves held-out attack success by about 30 percentage points on average over the strongest influence baseline. This is not a marginal gain; it indicates that set-level interactions dominate the optimization problem.

Third, the pipeline extends beyond one narrow setup. The paper reports transfer to code-generation backdoors, agentic backdoors on Qwen3-4B, and API-only finetuning of Kimi-K2.5. On SmolLM-360M, SAILS nearly matches an oracle-guided RL baseline while using much less cost. That comparison is especially informative for researchers interested in expensive training-defined objectives: learned surrogate ranking plus selective auditing can be more efficient than direct RL over the oracle.

The most useful ablation-level insight is conceptual rather than cosmetic. The reference model is treated as a common origin in behavioral space, and the allowed drift budget defines a local boundary. Within that neighborhood, drift magnitude determines distance from the origin, while direction determines how the limited behavioral change is allocated across capabilities. This gives a common coordinate system in which heterogeneous updates can be compared by directional efficiency: task improvement per unit of behavioral drift.

The second piece is a coarse but systematic layer-selective probe. Rather than introducing a complicated regularizer, the authors vary which layers are trainable while keeping the data, objective, and optimizer fixed as much as possible. This isolates accessible update directions as the main experimental variable. The result is that several layer subsets provide nearby directions that improve the QA-only target task while preserving reasoning and general capabilities. Full fine-tuning often fails because its large update space includes many easy loss-reducing directions that overwrite existing behaviors. LoRA also restricts directions, but its low-rank subspace does not consistently contain the efficient ones, so it helps in some settings and not in others.

Mechanistically, the paper argues that QA-only supervision specifies the answer but not the reasoning behavior. Optimization therefore tends to exploit whichever behavioral rewrite most easily reduces training loss. If the update space allows the model to bypass or compress its original reasoning style, standard SFT will often take that route. Layer selection changes the reachable subspace, nudging optimization toward adaptations that reuse rather than replace existing reasoning circuits.c2:T68e,The experiments use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, with scientific reasoning and multilingual translation as the main tasks. The layer-selective probe identifies multiple trainable-layer configurations that, at similar drift levels, improve the target task and preserve both reasoning and broader capabilities.

The deeper questions worth thinking about are whether the behavioral drift metric is robust to stylistic changes, and whether the good layer-selective directions truly preserve existing circuits or merely act as an implicit regularizer through reduced plasticity.c4:Tb9b,方法从 on-policy distillation 出发，但关键不是普通 teacher-student KL，而是“能力组合”的表示方式。作者对每个 specialist 构造一个 anchor pair：一个是 post-training 前的基线模型，一个是经过某种专项训练后的 specialist。对于同一个 token state，specialist 相对 anchor-before 的 log probability ratio 被视为该专项训练带来的 policy shift。这样定义有两个好处。第一，它抽取的是增量能力，而不是把 teacher 的全部分布都搬过来，因此更容易和其他 specialist 的增量叠加。第二，它不要求不同教师参数同构，只要求能在 student 生成的状态上打分。

在多能力组合时，Lightning Weave先把不同 anchor pair 的 log-ratio shift 对齐到 student 的 token states 上，再做加权求和，得到一个联合 shift。这里的设计选择很重要：作者不是分别构造多个 target 再做混合，而是先组合 shift，再构造单一目标分布。这样所有能力源在每个 token 决策点上共同作用，避免后续 target averaging 带来的不一致。

真正的方法核心是 Tilted-Target DOPD。作者指出，若直接把 DOPD 的 sampled-token surrogate 用在缓存轨迹上，会出现 stationary target 不保真的问题。原因是缓存来自旧的 behavior policy，当 student 更新后，基于缓存 action 估计的 regularizer 不再等价于当前 student 相对目标策略的 KL；即使 student 已经到达理想 shifted policy，loss 仍可能非零，梯度也不会消失，训练会继续把模型推离目标。为了解决这个问题，作者让每个缓存 shift 显式“倾斜”冻结的 behavior policy，构造出一个明确的 tilted target distribution，然后最小化当前 student 到该 target 的 KL。这样做后，至少在缓存状态上，目标是静态且可达的：当 student 匹配 target 时，loss 和梯度都应消失。文中还强调，这个构造保留了 token-level DOPD surrogate 在初始阶段的期望更新方向，因此既继承了原方法的有效起步信号，又修复了离线训练后期的目标漂移。

工程上，这个框架把昂贵的多教师在线打分转成一次性缓存。若有 K 个 anchor pair，在线 OPD 需要每条 student rollout 经过最多 2K 个 anchor 模型评分；Lightning Weave则先对缓存轨迹离线打分，之后训练只依赖 student 和缓存分数。这样多能力组合的成本主要前置到数据准备阶段，训练期更接近普通离线蒸馏。

与已有多教师蒸馏相比，这篇工作的区别不只是“多加几个 teacher”，而是把 teacher 的贡献限制为可解释的 policy shift，并为离线组合提供了一个有明确定点的目标分布。与参数空间 merge 相比，它不要求模型结构或参数对齐；与直接监督最终 specialist 相比，它更容易调节不同能力的权重，形成一条可控的 trade-off 曲线。c5:T9ae,The method starts from on-policy distillation, but the key idea is how capabilities are encoded. For each specialist, the authors form an anchor pair: a checkpoint before the relevant post-training stage and the resulting specialist after that stage. At a shared token state, the log-probability ratio between the specialist and the pre-stage anchor is treated as the policy shift learned during post-training. This is a useful abstraction because it isolates the incremental behavior change rather than copying the specialist distribution wholesale, and it does not require parameter alignment across teachers.

For multi-capability composition, Lightning Weave aligns these log-ratio shifts on student-generated token states and takes a weighted sum to form a joint shift. Importantly, it composes shifts first and constructs a single target distribution afterward, rather than building separate targets and averaging them later. That means all capability sources jointly shape each student decision at the token level.

The main technical contribution is Tilted-Target DOPD. The paper argues that directly reusing DOPD’s sampled-token surrogate on cached trajectories does not preserve the intended stationary solution. The cache was generated under an older behavior policy, and once the student moves away from that policy, the sampled-action regularizer no longer matches the KL that should be imposed relative to the current student. As a result, even if the student reaches the desired shifted policy, the cached surrogate can still produce non-zero gradients and push the model away from the solution. To fix this, each cached shift is used to explicitly tilt the frozen behavior policy into a target distribution, and training minimizes KL from the current student to that explicit target. This gives the offline objective a proper fixed point: when the student matches the target on cached states, both loss and gradient vanish. The paper also argues that this construction preserves the expected initial update direction of token-level DOPD, so it keeps the useful early-stage signal while repairing the late-stage mismatch.

From a systems perspective, the framework converts expensive online multi-teacher scoring into a one-time offline caching step. With K anchor pairs, naive online OPD may require up to 2K anchor-model evaluations per student rollout. Lightning Weave scores cached trajectories once and then trains using only the student and cached scores.c6:T590,The experiments cover both math and code reasoning, with student models including at least Qwen3-4B and Qwen3.5-4B, evaluated on five benchmarks. The main setting composes an accuracy-oriented shift from Klear with an efficiency-oriented shift from DECS. The reported results show consistent improvements in the accuracy–efficiency trade-off over both the base model and single-anchor alternatives.

The clearest numbers are as follows. On Qwen3-4B, Lightning Weave improves AIME 2024 accuracy from 72.9% to 76.0% while reducing response tokens by 21.3%. On Qwen3.5-4B, it improves HMMT 2025 accuracy from 59.2% to 64.0% with 10.7% fewer tokens, and LiveCodeBench v5 accuracy from 41.7% to 54.2% with 9.6% fewer tokens. These are meaningful because the gains are not coming from simply allowing longer traces, nor from sacrificing too much accuracy for brevity.

The weight-sweep results are also important. By varying the relative strengths of the anchor signals, the method produces a family of students that trace out an empirical Pareto frontier. That supports the claim that capabilities are genuinely composable and tunable, rather than the method working only at one lucky operating point. The most important ablations to inspect are the comparison between direct cached DOPD and Tilted-Target DOPD, the effect of composing shifts before target construction, and the trade-off curves under different anchor weights.c7:T60f,VG-OPD has two layers of selection: criterion-level expert eligibility and token-level supervision placement.

For the who question, each prompt comes with a rubric made of criteria, verifiers, and weights. Instead of collapsing the rubric into a single scalar reward and discarding structure, the method scores both the student rollout and each candidate expert answer with the same criterion-specific verifier. An expert is allowed to teach a criterion only if it shows a verified advantage over the student on that criterion for the current sample. This is a local, sample-specific notion of expertise, not a fixed domain prior.

For the which question, even an eligible expert does not supervise the whole sequence. The method identifies positions where the expert disagrees with the student and applies distillation only on those tokens through a sparse mask. The intuition is simple: if the student already matches the expert, there is little value in forcing additional imitation; the useful signal lies where the expert would actually change the student’s local decision.

Training remains inside an on-policy RL loop. The base policy update uses a rubric-based GRPO-style objective on the student’s own rollouts. The distillation term is a token-level reverse-KL estimate, but its weight is no longer uniform. It is gated by verifier-based eligibility and by the disagreement mask. In that sense, prompt-level multi-expert OPD methods such as MOPD appear as a special case with fixed teacher assignment and dense, uniform token weighting.c8:T563,The setup uses four RL-trained specialist experts and evaluates 4B and 8B students on seven benchmarks spanning scientific reasoning, domain science, and general reasoning. The headline numbers reported in the paper are that, at 4B, VG-OPD improves average accuracy over rubric-GRPO by 2.0 points on scientific reasoning and 3.3 points on domain science, while consistently outperforming coarse-grained MOPD. The 8B student shows the same pattern and achieves the best overall performance across the evaluation suite.

The ablations are the most informative part. The paper claims that both components matter: verifier-based expert eligibility and selective token supervision. That is an important result because the two mechanisms solve different failure modes. Eligibility answers whether a teacher should be trusted at all on a given criterion. Token masking answers where that trusted signal should be applied. Removing either one should reintroduce noisy supervision.

When reading the experiments, it is worth checking a few details: sensitivity to the number and quality of criteria, sparsity of the supervision mask, and whether multiple experts are actually used within a single problem. If expert switching happens frequently inside one answer, that would support the paper’s central claim that capability integration needs finer routing than prompt-level assignment.c9:T8fa,The method has two stages: attack discovery and attack generalization.

In the discovery stage, the authors use an investigator-agent elicitation framework in the standard hint-based monitorability setting. In that setup, a hint pointing toward an incorrect answer is appended to a multiple-choice problem, and the monitor checks whether the actor relied on the hint without acknowledging it. The interesting finding is that the investigator does not merely learn to suggest the wrong answer. It learns to inject a faulty but benign-sounding chain of reasoning. Even without an explicit instruction to follow it, the actor often paraphrases the injected plan inside its own CoT and reaches the wrong conclusion.

In the generalization stage, this observation is turned into a broader attack class called plan injection. The paper evaluates it in two harder settings: APPS coding backdoors and bio/math disguised-answer injection. In the coding case, the attack steers the model toward flawed or backdoored implementations. In the bio/math case, the attack uses superficially reasonable analysis to push the model toward an incorrect answer. A notable detail is that the injected content can be framed as an optional plan suggestion rather than a hard instruction, yet the actor still adopts it at high rates.

For monitoring, the paper compares thinking and non-thinking monitors. Thinking monitors are allowed to reason before judging; non-thinking monitors are closer to direct classification. Thinking monitors are stronger on average, but not robustly so. In some cases, extra reasoning budget causes the monitor to spend more tokens rationalizing the actor’s faulty reasoning instead of flagging it. The paper also tests whether giving the monitor access to the injected plan helps. On Bio-Math, it can actually reduce detection by as much as 50%, suggesting that more context can contaminate the monitor rather than assist it.

Relative to prior work, the novelty is that the actor is not explicitly instructed to hide malicious intent, nor is it fine-tuned to evade oversight. The attack exploits the model’s tendency to trust and internalize reasoning found in context. That makes the resulting trace look clean, because the suspicious planning has effectively been outsourced upstream.ca:T55e,Several empirical results stand out.

First, the attack transfers across scale. It is initially discovered on a 7B model, then shown to transfer to an 8B model and to DeepSeek-R1-0528 at 671B parameters. Larger scale does not remove the vulnerability.

Second, steering success is high. Plan injection drives the target behavior on over 80% of APPS attempts and over 90% of bio/math attempts. That indicates a strong tendency to adopt ready-made plans from context.

Third, monitor evasion remains substantial. Across monitorability benchmarks, the paper reports 25-33% evasion rates. Non-thinking monitors can miss up to 76% of attacks, and even the strongest monitor misses at least 25%.

Fourth, more monitor compute is not always better. The paper presents cases where additional thinking budget is spent explaining away the corrupted reasoning rather than detecting it. Another concrete result is that, on Bio-Math, giving the monitor access to the injected plan can reduce detection by up to 50%. That is important because many system designs assume that exposing more context to the monitor should help.

Stage 1 is Q-guided sample refinement. Given a state, the current flow policy maps Gaussian noise to an action. Instead of using that action directly, the method runs a finite number of MALA steps starting from the policy sample, targeting the Boltzmann distribution induced by the critic, p(a|s) proportional to exp(Q(s,a)/alpha). This is a practical choice: the method does not try to sample exactly from the target distribution, nor does it directly regress a critic-derived velocity field. It first generates a plausible action with the current policy, then uses critic gradients plus Metropolis correction to refine it toward higher-probability regions.

Stage 2 is self-target flow matching. The refined action is paired with the original base noise used to generate the pre-refinement action, and this pair becomes a source-target example for conditional flow matching. In effect, the model learns to map the same latent noise to a better action next time. The targets are therefore self-generated and improved by finite-step MCMC, not provided by an external oracle.

Relative to prior work, the differences are clear. It does not rely on Q-weighted regression alone, does not require directly learning a score model for the target action distribution, and does not treat the critic merely as a weighting function. Instead, it uses MCMC as an intermediate refinement operator and then amortizes that refinement into the flow policy. The paper also includes an idealized distributional analysis showing monotonic improvement of a maximum-entropy objective and identifying the Q-induced energy distribution as a fixed point. That theory is not a full practical guarantee, but it explains why the refine-then-distill loop is sensible.d0:T4f8,The experiments have two roles. The synthetic-distribution experiments test whether RFPO can preserve multimodality and fit complex target geometries, which is important because Gaussian actors often collapse such structure. The online continuous-control experiments test whether that expressive policy class translates into better RL performance. The headline claim is that RFPO matches or outperforms a standard Gaussian-policy baseline on almost all tasks.

From the provided full text, several experimental facts are clear: the target policy is the Q-induced Boltzmann distribution; the temperature alpha controls concentration; refinement uses a finite number of MALA steps rather than long-run sampling; and the paper evaluates not only return but also how well the learned policy approximates the target distribution.

The diagnosis centers on how the so-called Lucky Hit mechanism behaves under different answer spaces. Standard TTRL implicitly assumes that if the model samples multiple reasoning trajectories, the correct answer is more likely to become the majority and therefore serve as a useful pseudo-label. The authors argue that this assumption is much more plausible in large free-form answer spaces, where incorrect trajectories tend to disperse across many distinct strings. In a small multiple-choice space, however, different wrong rationales can collide on the same wrong option, creating a false consensus that is then reinforced by training. The model becomes more answer-consistent without becoming more correct.

Based on this diagnosis, the paper proposes PROSE: Process Reward Guided Self-Training. PROSE keeps the basic test-time RL loop—sample trajectories on unlabeled test questions, compute rewards, update the policy—but replaces majority-vote answer reward with process-level reward. A medical process reward model scores each reasoning step, and the trajectory reward is defined as the minimum step score rather than the mean. This design choice is central. Minimum aggregation prevents a trajectory from hiding one critical reasoning error behind many fluent or locally correct steps. If the weakest step is poor, the whole trajectory should not receive a high reward. The method also includes an answer-format guard to prevent reward hacking through malformed or strategically formatted outputs.

A practical aspect of the method is that the PRM is used only during adaptation, not at deployment-time inference. The goal is to internalize process supervision into the policy parameters rather than rely on an external reranker or verifier at test time. That distinguishes PROSE from many inference-time selection methods, which often improve quality at the cost of additional runtime modules and compute.d2:T836,The paper first shows the failure mode of standard TTRL on medical multiple-choice QA: sample-level accuracy improves only slightly, majority-vote accuracy stays flat, and output diversity drops sharply. In other words, the model becomes more self-consistent but not more correct.

The most convincing experiment is the controlled answer-space intervention. On AMC math problems, the authors keep the questions, model, optimizer, and training procedure fixed, and vary only the answer format: original free-form answering versus a matched four-option multiple-choice version. In the free-form setting, TTRL improves steadily. In the multiple-choice setting, accuracy rises briefly and then collapses. This strongly supports the claim that answer-space structure, not domain difficulty, is the main cause of failure.

The paper also introduces the protection gap, which measures the difference between pseudo-label reward accuracy and true answer accuracy. In free-form answer spaces, this gap provides some protection because wrong answers disperse. In small answer spaces, the gap nearly disappears, making it much easier for wrong trajectories to be rewarded through majority agreement. This quantitative analysis supports the Lucky Hit diagnosis.

Empirically, PROSE improves both sample-level and majority-vote accuracy relative to standard TTRL and avoids the rapid diversity collapse. Two additional findings matter. Second, the gains transfer to datasets that were not used during adaptation, suggesting that the method learns more general reasoning behavior rather than dataset-specific answer preferences. The main challenge is not the existence of labels, but how to make those labels valid. The paper identifies three constraints. First, supervision must be applied under rollout-consistent draft-conditioned states. The k-th drafted token is predicted conditioned on previous drafted tokens, not on the final executed prefix after verification. To avoid train-test mismatch, GrowMTP records the draft trajectory and reconstructs the hidden states corresponding to the actual draft-conditioned context that produced each proposal. Second, learning across drafting depths is coupled. A deeper token only matters if earlier drafted tokens are accepted, so depth-wise training should reflect that dependency rather than treating each position as an independent classification target. The paper introduces a depth-coupled acceptance (DCA) loss based on an acceptance-chain surrogate, with a logarithmic transform to increase relative gradient weight on low-chain-value cases. Third, supervision beyond the first rejection is invalid for execution, because deeper drafted tokens are conditioned on a rejected token and therefore lie off the executed prefix. GrowMTP gates the loss after the first rejection and excludes those suffix positions. A further design choice is to detach draft-head updates from the policy backbone, so the online drafting module does not directly perturb policy learning. This sacrifices possible gains from joint optimization, but keeps the method modular and stable. An important practical point is that no offline warm start or depth curriculum is required: the first draft position always yields valid supervision, so training can begin from random initialization.d5:T4a3,The headline result is from-scratch online growth on a headless model. For a given prefix, they sample multiple independent continuations from the same policy and average the terminal rewards. These MC values reveal local changes in expected success along a trajectory. When compared with the PPO critic, the MC values often show sharp transitions, while critic predictions remain smooth and sometimes move in the wrong direction. A controlled stochastic FrozenLake experiment isolates the phenomenon further: as the maze size grows, the critic becomes smoother and less accurate. The analysis identifies two causes. First, in terminal-only reward settings, the standard token-level critic MSE contains an implicit penalty on variation among values within the same response, which encourages a flatter profile. Second, neighboring LLM states share almost all prefix tokens, so their representations and critic gradients are similar; dense supervision aggregates many near-duplicate updates and further pulls nearby predictions together. The paper notes that this is related to GRPO but does not use PPO clipping. Those are the parts with the most value for speech LM and multimodal post-training research.db:T76d,PIVOT is a dual-level learning framework. The first part is trajectory-level anchoring. Instead of turning the problem into generic off-policy RL, the method builds a self-calibrated replay pool that stores historical responses judged to be both visually grounded and reasoning-stable. Visual grounding is estimated through a counterfactual measure: compare the model’s predictive distribution under the original image and a corrupted image, and use the KL divergence as a proxy for visual dependency. If the trajectory changes a lot when the image is corrupted, it likely relies on visual evidence rather than language priors. Stability is approximated by average trajectory entropy, motivated by prior observations that lower-entropy trajectories tend to be more reliable under RLVR. These replayed trajectories are used as retrospective anchors, not as hard imitation targets, so the method tries to preserve useful behavior without collapsing exploration.

The second part is token-level anchoring through vision-guided advantage allocation. Standard DAPO/GRPO-style methods broadcast one sequence-level advantage to all tokens. PIVOT instead estimates token importance using counterfactual visual support and each token’s effect on future reasoning. Tokens that appear more visually grounded or more consequential for downstream reasoning receive stronger optimization weight. The PPO-style clipped objective remains, but the advantage becomes token-modulated rather than uniform.

Relative to prior work, the differences are clear. It does not merely replay successful samples; it filters replay candidates using visual dependency and stability. It does not stop at sequence-level reranking; it pushes credit assignment down to tokens. And it does not require extra annotation or a new verifier, relying instead on counterfactual signals extracted from the model’s own multimodal behavior.dc:T500,From the available full-text excerpt, the experimental setup spans multiple data scales and model scales, with consistent gains over standard multimodal RLVR baselines, likely including DAPO-style group-based policy optimization.
